Abstract:
Abstract:

The present invention relates to a fault diagnosis system for electric vehicle motors. The system integrates multiple sensors (current, voltage, vibration, temperature, and acoustic) to monitor motor health in real time. A data acquisition unit (DAQ) collects sensor data, which is processed by a microcontroller unit (MCU) to extract key fault-related features. The processed data is analyzed by a machine learning model, leveraging deep learning techniques such as CNNs and RNNs to detect and classify faults like winding failures, rotor misalignment, and insulation damage. A wireless communication module transmits diagnostic data to a cloud-based platform or mobile application for remote monitoring. The system includes predictive maintenance capabilities, enabling early fault detection and minimizing downtime. Designed for high-speed, safety-critical applications, this invention ensures robust, real-time fault diagnosis, enhancing the operational efficiency and longevity of EV motors.

TECHNICAL FIELD OF INVENTION

The present invention is related to the field of electrical engineering. More specifically, it relates to a fault diagnosis system for electric vehicle motors. 

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

The background information herein below relates to the present disclosure but is not necessarily prior art.

Switched reluctance motors (SRMs) have attracted much attention in industry due to the advantages of low cost, robust structure, high fault tolerance and high torque density. However, several disadvantages like high torque ripples and coil temperatures hinder their industrialization for some applications requiring high dynamic performance, like electric vehicles (EVs). A minimal current sensing strategy and fault detection of SRMs is presented in. In order to reduce the number of required current sensors in multiphase motor drives, the optimal selection and location of current sensors is presented in consideration of the precise actual phase current measurement, open- and short-circuit fault detection. 

The proposed scheme requires two current sensors to replace the phase current sensors placed in each phase without any additional devices for multiphase SRMs to achieve a more compact and low-cost drive. Different current regulation methods are employed for single phase conducting region and commutation region. To obtain the phase currents from the proposed approach, different settings of the pulse-width modulation (PWM) signals for adjacent phases during the commutation region are implemented. The simulation and experiments on a four-phase 8/6 pole SRM are carried out to verify the effectiveness of this approach in the healthy and faulty cases.  A new current sensor placement algorithm of SRMs with enhanced fault-detection capability has been presented in. This technique uses the optimal current sensor placement to reduce the number of required current sensors, and to allow for the measurement of the phase currents and detection of different types of faults. Soft chopping is used during the single-phase conducting period whereas employing the hard chopping during the commutation region. 

Different PWM settings of the adjacent phases are required to implement the current separation. According to the simulation and experimental results, the phase currents obtained by the proposed current sensors are able to achieve a good agreement with the measured currents at the phase outputs under load and speed transients. Furthermore, the proposed approach can effectively detect open- and short-circuit faults through a general algorithm that provides information on the fault type and location without any extra devices and the consequential increase of the system complexity and costs.

The challenge of minimizing the unbalanced magnetic pull caused during a single pole failure, which is the most common electrical fault found in SRMs is addressed in. In fault tolerant SRMs usually the entire faulty phase is turned-off to continue operation. To minimize the loss of torque production during fault, a distributed inverter (one inverter module per coil) is introduced enabling the SRM to continue operation with all remaining healthy poles. Furthermore, a fault tolerant control strategy utilizing the advantages of the distributed inverter namely radial force minimization control is proposed. 

This control allows considerable reduction in the unbalanced magnetic pull, while maintaining constant torque control during faulty operation. A four phase 1kW 16/12 SRM with a distributed inverter is used to present the theoretical approach and simulation results of the proposed control algorithm. Furthermore, experimental measurement results for the radial force minimization control are shown to validate the effectiveness of the introduced algorithm. To create a highly reliable SRM drive system a single pole fault ride through with continued control of the output torque has been presented. In addition to torque control, the unbalanced magnetic pull (UMP) which is produced due to loss of symmetry amongst the radial forces in the faulty phase, is minimized. A radial force minimization control (RFMC) used in conjunction with pulse width modulation direct instantaneous torque control (PWM-DITC) is proposed. 

The proposed RFMC algorithm has shown in simulation and test bench measurements that the control can deliver the required output torque while reducing the UMP significantly. Moreover, compared to elementary fault control (EFC), the increment observed in thermal loading of the functional poles belonging to the faulty phase is lower. This enables RFMC to be used over a wide operating range. The actual range is determined by the maximum allowed thermal loading of the machine in the application during the fault condition. A reduction in the experimentally determined UMP larger than 73%, from a peak value of 370N to values well below 100N, could be observed. Therefore, adding a distributed inverter and the RFMC algorithm enables fault tolerant SRM operation during single pole faults.

A sensorless control strategy with one-phase lacking fault-tolerant capability is proposed in for the SRM. This strategy consists of a phase inductance slope zero-crossing detection scheme and a series of phase inductance partition logic algorithms, which is capable of capturing at least one-phase aligned position under both normal operation and one-phase lacking fault operation. With the recorded index position in each electric period, the rotor position can be estimated for sensorless driving accordingly. To ensure stable calculation of the phase inductance in this method, the SRM should be started and operated under single pulse control mode. 

Thus, for sensorless starting, an idle phase inductance double threshold based sensorless synthetic starting scheme is also developed. The proposed strategy is easy for implementation and can ensure stable sensorless operation in full speed range. Moreover, it does not need any priori measuring process, complicated logic algorithm or complex mathematical calculation. The theoretical analysis is conducted, and experimental results are provided to verify the feasibility of the proposed control strategy. The inter-turn short-circuit fault of stator winding is a common failure mode in SRMs, which can severely harm the operation of the motor. A novel method for diagnosing the inter-turn short-circuit fault in the current chopping mode is proposed in, which is suitable for online monitoring and protection of SRMs. The proposed method achieves a fast response and high sensitivity and can mitigate the interference of load conditions on detection reliability. Moreover, this method is based on phase currents, which does not require additional sensor or detection circuits. 

Meanwhile, the effects of inter-turn fault location in the stator winding on the motor flux and motor parameters are analyzed in detail through finite element analysis, which is helpful to establish a reliable diagnostics technique for various fault conditions. Experimentations based on an 8/6 four-phase SRM with special windings designed to simulate inter-turn short circuit conditions are conducted, and the results have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

A multi-sensor data fusion method is investigated in for bearing fault diagnosis of a SRM of an electric vehicle (EV) powertrain under varying speed conditions. The accumulative rotation angle of the SRM rotor is estimated by fusing the synchronous sampled current and vibration signals. The time-domain vibration signal is then resampled on an angular domain, and the bearing fault type is identified on the envelope spectrum of the resampled signal. An experimental setup is designed to validate the performance of the proposed method compared with the traditional ones. 

The practical EV working conditions including driving, coasting, and braking are considered in the experiments. Results indicated that the proposed method successfully diagnoses the SRM bearing faults under random and complex conditions. The method is promising for online SRM fault diagnosis under varying speed conditions as it requires no extra tachometer, specifically when the sensorless control strategy is adopted.

A position pulse signal fault diagnosis scheme based on synthetic hybrid-integral-threshold logic is proposed in for SRM drives. In this method, the complementary position pulse signals of each sensor are used as the independent reference signals. By applying special integral calculations on each reference signals and capturing their rising and falling edges respectively, the position pulse fault cases like high-level and low-level faults can be diagnosed immediately with the synthetic thresholds comparison logic. 

To verify the validity of the proposed method, a 1kW 12/8 structure SRM prototype with three independent hall sensors installed is used as a test machine. Experimental results show that this method can diagnose the position fault of each position sensor independently and ensure very fast position fault detection even under dynamic operations with speed transients. Furthermore, the method can be implemented without additional hardware and complex computation, which is quite suitable for constructing a reliable position measurement module to assist the rotor position sensors.

Power converter is critical but prone to be failure in SRM drives. The open and short-circuit fault characteristics of freewheeling diode in asymmetric bridge power converter are analyzed in details. Based on logic judgment, four online fault diagnostic methods with digital phase current analysis of power converter are proposed in. The fault features are extracted by analyzing the relationship between chopping signal and the current information from some special positions. 

The four fault diagnostic methods are carried out according to the current obtained by detecting dc bus current and the lower freewheeling bus current, the chopped bus current, the upper excitation bus current and lower freewheeling bus current, the lower excitation bus current, and dc bus current, respectively. Comparisons between the four diagnostic methods are conducted. Simulations and experiments on a 12/8 SRM validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods. 

A novel reliability evaluation scheme to achieve quantitative reliability calculation for power converter in the whole operation region of SRM system is presented in. Firstly, the electrical model is built to obtain electrical stress and fault-tolerance capability in Matlab/Simulink environment. Secondly, thermal circuit model is performed to get the thermal stress of power converter quickly. Thirdly, dynamical Markov model with a novel failure criterion is applied to achieve quantitative reliability calculation by characterizing the fault-tolerance capability and thermal stress. The proposed failure criterion can simplify the model to decrease the number of states and avoid the divergence of results. 

Especially the interconnected relationship of the three models is key emphasized. Next, the proposed reliability evaluation scheme is carried out to explore the reliability of power converter under different chopping modes. Finally, simulations in conjunction with experiment verifies the validity of the proposed reliability evaluation scheme.

The characteristics of a dual three-phase synchronous motor under different operating conditions such as healthy, half-control, and post fault conditions is compared in. The inductances are analyzed to confirm the interaction between two three phase systems, and induced voltages of each phase are measured to verify the interaction behaviors. The post fault characteristics are analyzed under open-circuit faults (single-open-switch and single-open-phase faults) and short-circuit faults (single short-switch and one-three-phase-short faults). 

The predicted results are validated by experimental tests. Moreover, the half-control mode is investigated as a strategy to operate with high efficiency and tolerant mode. An online fault diagnosis (FD) algorithm is developed in to detect stator’s turn-to-turn faults (TTFs) in direct torque control (DTC) driven IMs for the electric vehicles (EV) power-trains. The developed FD algorithm is based on the application of the discrete wavelet transformation (DWT) technique on the stator currents. 

Being a time-frequency domain based algorithm, DWT can deal with non-stationary signals. The fault-sensitive decomposition levels were selected using Ostu’s thresholding formulation to detect the stator’s faults at their embryonic stage. To determine the faulty phase, the concept of differential discrete wavelet energy (DDWE) was introduced. A finite element (FE) co-simulation platform and experimental setup were built to examine the proposed FD algorithm. The results depicted the robustness of the FD method. A comparative analysis is presented between the developed DDWE based FD, and the conventional motor current signature analysis (MCSA)-based FD. The experimental results proved that developed FD is faster and more accurate than the MCSA based FD one. Moreover, the presented FD routine was examined under load step-change and intermittent TTFs, and its diagnosing effectiveness was verified. 

SRM drives are one competitive technology for traction motor drives. A novel and flexible SRM fault-tolerant topology with fault diagnosis, fault tolerance, and advanced control functions is proposed in. The converter is composed of a single-phase bridge and a relay network, based on the traditional asymmetrical half-bridge driving topology. When the SRM-driving system is subjected to fault conditions including open-circuit and short-circuit faults, the proposed converter starts its fault-diagnosis procedure to locate the fault. Based on the relay network, the faulty part can be bypassed by the single-phase bridge arm, while the single-phase bridge arm and the healthy part of the converter can form a fault-tolerant topology to sustain the driving operation. 

A fault-tolerant control strategy is developed to decrease the influence of the fault. Furthermore, the proposed fault-tolerant strategy can be applied to three-phase 12/8 SRM and four-phase 8/6 SRM. Simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink and experiments on a three-phase 12/8 SRM and a four-phase 8/6 SRM validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy, which may have significant economic implications in traction drive systems. The developed technology can improve the reliability and cost efficiency of the SRM drive for EV/HEVs, as well as electric aircraft and ships.

The switched reluctance (SR) drive is known to be fault tolerant, but it is not fault free. The goals of are the systematic classification of all electrical faults, for short and open circuits, in the SR drive (excluding the controller itself) and the investigation of fault patterns and possible remediation. Each situation is analyzed via finite-element analysis and/or experiments. The transient effects during the faults are described. Possible remediation schemes other than disabling the faulted phase are explored. There is a particular focus on the switch short circuit for which new results are presented. The findings, although demonstrated on relatively small motors, are explained in such a way that they are anticipated to be valid, regardless of the motor rating.

A new open-end winding induction motor (OEWIM)-based dual-motor differential four-wheel drive (D4WD) for the electric vehicle (EV) is presented in. Constant speed operation through cruise control is achieved using direct torque control (DTC) algorithm. The redundant vectors are used in the switching vector selection of the DTC algorithm to achieve balanced battery currents. Fault-tolerant operation (FTO) of the drive is demonstrated, where the EV will work with full torque even if one of the inverters in rear motor drive or front motor drive or both fail. 

The dynamic model of the proposed drive is presented. The proposed drive and FTO are verified through simulation as per the FTP-75 driving cycle. An experimental prototype of the proposed drive is developed, and the abovementioned algorithms are verified experimentally as per the FTP-75 and highway (HFET) driving cycles. Both the simulation and experimental results are presented, and these results agree with the theoretical observations. Stable operation of EV for the entire test cycle under normal operation, as well as inverter fault conditions, is demonstrated. The proposed drive train arrangement will find applications in high-power electric ground vehicles, all-electric ships, and all-electric aircraft. It is more suited for urban areas, hilly terrain, and remote locations where FTO of EVs is desired. 

Distributed battery packs, battery power management under FTO, the use of advanced artificial intelligence algorithms for switching vector selection, and battery management are some of the interesting works for the future. Extending the work to next higher power-level EVs with multilevel inverter feeding OEWIM drives with distributed battery and enhanced power management will be a challenging research work for the future. Another interesting area of further research is the investigation of the impact of EV slip control in the case of inverter loss.

A multiobjective and multiphysics design optimization method considering both thermal and electromagnetic performance is presented in [15] for a 12/10 SRM. First, the topology of the SRM is introduced and the optimal parameters are defined. Then, the electromagnetic finite element model (FEM) is introduced and the improved transient lumped-parameter thermal model (TLPTM), considering both axial and radial heat transfer for the SRM, is proposed. Second, the objectives and constraints of the optimization are determined. 

To improve the optimization efficiency, the sequential subspace optimization strategy is employed to find the optimal solution of this high-dimensional design optimization problem. Finally, to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, both simulation and experimental results are given and discussed. Compared with the initial design, the optimal solution exhibits lower temperature, higher torque, lower torque ripple and less loss.

In a near future when Industry 4.0 is implanted, predictive maintenance will have a much more prominent role than that currently plays in traditional industry. Predictive maintenance is the organized monitoring with periodic or continuous measurement of variables of the state of the equipment to be maintained and its comparison with pre-established patterns for the determination of the instant in which the maintenance intervention should take place. 

Three-phase induction motor drives are one of the industrial equipment that has been given greater attention regarding predictive maintenance plans. In recent years, SRM drives have begun to have some relevance in the industry. After a brief review of the SRMs and their control, an analysis of the different types of faults and a description of the most usual diagnostic techniques in electric drives, a predictive maintenance plan for switched reluctance motor drives is proposed in. This predictive maintenance plan considers different control strategies (hysteresis and single pulse), and is based on diagnostic techniques such as analysis of currents and spectral analysis of vibrations. Exhaustive experimental tests have been carried out in order to validate the proposed plan.

A simplified 3D magneto-thermal model is presented in to study the temperature distribution over the housing of a SRM. The main objective of such model is to study the temperature distribution profile on the body of the machine under various working conditions in order to introduce a temperature based signature to develop condition monitoring procedures. The analysis of fluid flow and heat transfer inside the SRM supports the hypothesis that the effect of turbulent flow of the fluid and the complex heat transfer phenomenon of the rotating parts can be simplified to a heat flux boundary condition representation of the heat loss. 

The accuracy of the model is validated through simulation and experimental results on a prototype SRM. The developed simplified model can be used as for prediction of temperature profile on SRM surface, well suited for fault diagnosis in SRM. The proposed methodology can be modified applied in developing a thermal model for other types of electric machines.

 A novel modular full-bridge converter is proposed in for three-phase switched reluctance motors (SRMs), which provides an advanced fault-tolerance solution for both the open- and short-circuit faults in switching devices. The proposed converter is composed of two standard six-pack switch modules, providing great benefits for industrial massive production due to the modular topology. Under normal conditions, bidirectional current excitation is developed in the proposed converter, where all the switching devices are actively involved, which makes full use of the switches and averages the heat dissipation for the heat sink design. 

When a switch fault occurs, the fault signature can be extracted by detecting the characteristics of phase currents and operation modes, and effective fault-tolerance strategies are further applied to achieve the fault tolerance operation accordingly. Under switch open-circuit faults, the faulty phase is adjusted to unidirectional current excitation without degrading the motor performance. Under switch short-circuit faults, the motor can still work steadily with a single six-switch inverter module by easily reconstructing the proposed converter, without losing any phase windings. The simulation and experiments on a three-phase 12/8 SRM are carried out to validate the feasibility of the proposed converter and control techniques.

Implementation of fault diagnosis for power converter is critical to improve the reliability of electric vehicle (EV) with SRM drive. Conventional fault diagnosis methods are usually suitable for a single chopping mode or a certain control strategy. To avoid the problem, a virtual current coefficients based diagnosis method for power transistors is proposed considering different chopping modes, different control strategies, and different fault cases simultaneously. The multi-point current detection method is proposed in to obtain more current information, which is capable of providing remarkable fault features. The sensor current variations under various fault conditions are analyzed. 

The fault is firstly detected by identifying the error between the real sensor current and the value calculated with the mixed logic model. Three virtual current coefficients are introduced to obtain the fault location principles. The fault types and fault power transistors are recognized according to the difference between the real current coefficients and the virtual current coefficients. The applications of the fault diagnosis method are extended with the proposed scheme. The method does not require complex calculation, and thus has a good dynamic performance. Experiments on a three-phase 12/8 SRM drive validate the effectiveness of the proposed fault diagnosis method.

The performance and reliability of a cost-effective novel integrated power converter (NIPC) are investigated in [20] in comparison to the asymmetric half-bridge power converter (AHBPC) for switched reluctance drive (SRD) system. First, with the soft chopping manner, the working modes and voltage equations of NIPC are illustrated to develop the conventional control strategies. Second, given that the power switches are the reliability-critical devices of converters, a novel control strategy is put forward to shorten the operation time and lower the electrical stress of power switches. Besides, the SRD system with NIPC can still operate with the faults of power switches, especially the output torque of faulty phase is not zero when the open-circuit fault happens. 

But in order to further enlarge the output torque of faulty phase and lower the torque ripple, the fault-tolerance strategy is proposed. Next, to effectively evaluate the topologies from the perspective of reliability, a unified Markov model is introduced to conduct the static and dynamic reliability analysis, illustrating that the reliability of NIPC is evidently higher than AHBPC. Finally, the simulation and experiments on a prototype SRD system are developed to verify the effectiveness of proposed NIPC and corresponding control strategies.

A novel reliability assessment scheme is presented in to achieve the optimal selection of control strategies for SRM system from the perspective of reliability. To begin with, a combination model of k-out-of-n:G model and Markov model is proposed to lower the complexity and enhance the accuracy of system-level reliability assessment. As for the component-level reliability assessment, the three-dimensional coupled thermal circuit model of power converter is built to achieve the precise and fast prediction of junction temperature that is necessary for calculation of failure rate. 

Then the static and dynamic reliability analysis are carried out under voltage chopping control (VCC), current chopping control (CCC) and angle position control (APC) strategies, which indicates the implementation scope of APC strategy should be broadened. Compared with VCC strategy, CCC strategy is strongly recommended even if current sensors boost the extra failure rate. Besides, the increase in redundancy levels on power converter is certified as the most powerful measure for reliability enhancement of SRM system. 

The most cost-effective redundancy level can also be quantitatively obtained. The experiments of fault-tolerance capability and thermal stress indirectly verify the validity of reliability analysis. Electric drive system is a key subsystem of battery electric vehicles (BEVs). Abnormalities in the electric drive system components may lead to performance degradation in the drive system, and more severely, loss of power in the vehicle. An integrated prognosis system is presented in for early detection and isolation of electric drive system and component faults. The system first calculates multiple health features, known as health indicators derived from the available on-board sensor signals. Then, an integrated prognostic and fault isolation strategy is used to isolate the root cause of electric drive faults by monitoring the performance of the multiple health indicators. 

The prognostic system uses a hierarchical approach: it first determines if there is a degradation in the electric drive system by comparing the system achieved torque with the estimated torque, and then goes further to check multiple component-level health indicators for the various components comprising an electric drive system, including motor stator winding, three phase current sensors and resolver. After a component has been detected to degrade to a certain level, the prognosis system sends out an alert before the severe performance reduction of the drive system occurs, thus protecting the customers from loss of propulsion and walk home situations.

A technical overview for fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant strategies of SRM systems is presented in. future research works and forecast research hotspots on fault diagnosis techniques are provided as follows: The fault detection process should be accelerated and more efficient signal processing scheme should be put forward; The computing burden of the controller should be reduced by applying simple and effective fault diagnosis method without affecting the normal operation of the SRM; The fault should be precisely located and failure spreading should be effectively prevented; and The detection sensors and other extra devices should be further reduced.

OBJECTIVE OF THE INVENTION

The primary objective of the present invention is to provide a fault diagnosis system for electric vehicle motors.  
Yet another objective of the invention is to investigate various types of motors used in EVs, including Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs), Brushless DC Motors (BLDC), and Induction Motors (IM).

Yet another objective of the invention is to identify and categorize different types of faults occurring in these motors, such as electrical, mechanical, thermal, and sensor faults.

Yet another objective of the invention is to determine the critical parameters needed for fault diagnosis, including voltage, current, vibration, temperature, and noise signals.

Yet another objective of the invention is to design and implement an intelligent fault detection model using machine learning techniques to accurately diagnose faults in EV motors.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

Accordingly the following invention provides a fault diagnosis system for electric vehicle motors.  The system integrates multiple sensors (current, voltage, vibration, temperature, and acoustic) to monitor motor health in real time. A data acquisition unit (DAQ) collects sensor data, which is processed by a microcontroller unit (MCU) to extract key fault-related features. The processed data is analyzed by a machine learning model, leveraging deep learning techniques such as CNNs and RNNs to detect and classify faults like winding failures, rotor misalignment, and insulation damage. 

A wireless communication module transmits diagnostic data to a cloud-based platform or mobile application for remote monitoring. The system includes predictive maintenance capabilities, enabling early fault detection and minimizing downtime. Designed for high-speed, safety-critical applications, this invention ensures robust, real-time fault diagnosis, enhancing the operational efficiency and longevity of EV motors.

The present invention is related to a fault diagnosis system for electric vehicle motors.  Over recent decades, electric vehicles (EVs) and hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) have attracted growing attention due to the low-pollution and high-efficiency characteristics, which provides a promising solution to the depletion of fossil fuels and environmental problems. For a propulsion machine in EVs and HEVs, switched reluctance motors (SRMs) are becoming one potential candidate for harsh environments due to their advantages of low cost, simple, and robust structure without permanent magnet, high reliability, and strong applicability.

There are considerable demands for developing electrical motors with high torque density, high efficiency and low cost for the propulsion of EVs. The SRMs is one of the competitive candidates for EVs, besides permanent magnet synchronous machines and induction machines, thanks to some significant advantages, such as simple structure, low cost, rare-earth free, rotor robustness, high reliability and inherent fault-tolerance ability. On the downside, severe torque ripple, noise and vibrations may be troublesome in some applications. 

SRMs are known for their simple and robust mechanical design, low magnetic pole and phase coupling as well as low short-circuit current and open circuit voltage during fault condition. These advantages make the SRM a suitable candidate for applications, which require high reliability and fault tolerant operation. SRMs have many advantages including robust construction, control flexibility, good operation environments adaptability, and excellent fault-tolerant capability. However, how to measure or estimate the rotor position reliably is still a challenge, especially when SRMs are operated under harsh or faulty conditions. As is well known, traditional position sensors are vulnerable to the environmental variables, such as the temperature, oil stains, humility, dust and etc. Thus, most of these sensors would become invalid in extreme environments and fault conditions, which makes it necessary to develop highly reliable sensorless schemes to improve the fault tolerant capability of the SRM drives.

Reliable rotor position measurement is quite necessary for ensuring accurate commutation control in many kinds of motor drives, such as SRM and brushless DC motor (BLDC). Traditionally, the hall sensors and photoelectric switch sensors are widely used in most of those low-cost motor drive systems. In these systems, the rotor position needs to be decoded from the discrete voltage pulses measured by the sensors. Thus, to develop an online position pulse signals fault diagnosis scheme with fast fault monitoring capability is quite vital for avoiding the abnormal driving control and improving the overall system reliability.

With the widespread utilization of electrical motors, stability and reliability become the most important considerations for safety. SRMs are famous for their great robustness, wide speed range, and high fault-tolerant capability, which are much suitable for high-speed and safety-critical applications. Although the SRM drive have some fault tolerance ability, the fault still seriously affects the system performance. The faults happening in different parts, such as converter, motor winding, sensors, and rotor, may lead to low torque, large torque ripple, overcurrent, insulation damage, and even system broken-down, without any fault-tolerant consideration. 

Therefore, it is important and urgent to improve the motor system reliability and robustness for SRM and other drives. The machine learning based fault diagnosis can change this problem with faster fault identification in motor of electric vehicles with the machine learning based models. The study focuses on analyzing various motors used in electric vehicles, identifying their characteristics and functionalities. It further examines potential faults that may occur in these motors, providing a comprehensive understanding of failure mechanisms. Additionally, existing fault diagnosis mechanisms for electric vehicle motors are reviewed to assess their effectiveness and limitations. 

Key parameters essential for fault diagnosis are identified to enhance accuracy and efficiency. Based on these parameters, a machine learning methodology is designed and developed for diagnosing faults in electric vehicle motors. Finally, the performance of the proposed methodologies is evaluated to ensure reliability and effectiveness in real-world applications. 

With the widespread utilization of electrical motors, stability and reliability become the most important considerations for safety. Different motors like SRMs, BLDC, IM, etc. are used in EVs. These motors are prone to various faults. The main objective of the proposed research work is to detect these faults for ensuring safety and proper functioning electric vehicles.

In the proposed research work a machine learning based fault diagnosis model for fault identification in motor of electric vehicles will be designed and analyzed. Initially various motors which can be used in electric vehicles will be explored. Then the different faults which can occur in these motors will be analyzed. The fault characteristics will be studied. The various parameters required for identification of different faults in the EVs motors will be identified and evaluated. The machine learning based model will be designed on the basis of these parameters. This model will be evaluated for different types of faults. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Workflow of System Model
[0036] The proposed system for virtual machine (VM) trading in a federated cloud environment is based on a multi-attribute double auction mechanism. The system is designed to handle complex bid and ask requests from multiple cloud service providers (CSPs) and customers, ensuring optimal resource allocation and pricing. The system model incorporates multiple functional modules that work together to execute the auction process, compute scoring values, match bids and asks, calculate clearing prices, and monitor overall system performance.
[0037] The system begins with the Bid and Ask Processing Module that receives bid and ask requests from CSPs and customers. Each bid and ask includes multi-attribute parameters such as processing power, memory, bandwidth, operational cost, and budget. The Scoring Function Module computes a scoring value for each bid and ask using a weighted linear combination of the defined parameters. This scoring value helps rank the bids and asks, ensuring that the most valuable and compatible resources are matched efficiently.
[0038] The Matching Module ranks and matches bids and asks based on the computed scoring values. If two or more pairs have similar scoring values, a priority-based mechanism is used to resolve ties. Once a match is identified, the Clearing Price Calculation Module determines the clearing price based on the operational cost and expected revenue, ensuring a balanced market-based approach.
[0039] To maximize the overall efficiency of the system, the Profit and Social Welfare Calculation Module computes the total profit generated from VM-job pairings and assesses social welfare by considering the utility value gained by the customers. The Adaptation and Learning Module dynamically adjusts the scoring function weights based on historical transaction data and market trends, ensuring that the system remains responsive to changing market conditions.
[0040] The Performance Monitoring Module tracks system metrics such as profit, social welfare, resource utilization, and response time. This allows the system to generate real-time performance reports, identify bottlenecks, and suggest optimizations. Finally, the Security and Privacy Module secures data transmission and storage using encryption and access control mechanisms, ensuring that all transactions and user data remain secure and protected from unauthorized access.
Algorithm of Multi-Attribute Based Double Auction
[0041] The multi-attribute based double auction follows a systematic process involving bid and ask submission, scoring, matching, and clearing price calculation. The process begins with CSPs submitting their bids and customers submitting their asks. Each bid and ask includes multi-attribute parameters like processing power, memory, bandwidth, operational cost, and budget. The scoring function computes a value based on the importance of each parameter, which is determined through pre-defined weights.
[0042] The matching process involves ranking bids and asks based on their computed scores. A priority-based tie-breaking mechanism is employed when multiple pairs have similar scores. The clearing price is then computed using a market-based approach that minimizes the difference between supply and demand. After successful matching, the system calculates the total profit and social welfare from the transaction.
[0043] The system uses machine learning techniques to update the scoring function weights based on historical data and market conditions. This ensures that the system remains adaptive and responsive to dynamic market trends. Performance metrics such as profit, social welfare, and resource utilization are continuously monitored to improve the system’s efficiency and reliability.
Mathematical Model
[0044] The system's mathematical foundation is based on the following key components:
Bid and Ask Definition:

Each bid Bi from CSPs and each ask Aj from customers is defined as:
Bi={Pi,Mi,Bi,Ci,Qi}
Aj={Pj,Mj,Bj,Cj,Qj} 
where P = processing power, M = memory, B = bandwidth, C = operational cost, Q = quality requirements.
Scoring Function:
The scoring function for bids and asks is computed as:
S(Bi)=w1Pi+w2Mi+w3Bi+w4Ci+w5Qi
S(Aj)=w1Pj+w2Mj+w3Bj+w4Cj+w5Qj
where w1,w2,w3,w4,w5 are pre-defined weights for each attribute.
Matching Function:
The matching function is defined as:
M(Bi,Aj)=max(S(Bi)-S(Aj))
The pair with the highest matching score is selected.
Clearing Price Calculation:
The clearing price for a matched pair is calculated as:
Pclear=(S(Bi)+S(Aj))/2
Profit and Social Welfare Calculation:
The total profit and social welfare are computed as:
Profit=?i,j(Pclear-Ci)
Social Welfare=?i,j(S(Aj)-Pclear)

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Cloud computing has become a critical enabler of modern digital infrastructure, offering scalable, on-demand access to computing resources. Businesses, enterprises, and service providers rely on cloud platforms to handle complex workloads, manage distributed applications, and optimize computational efficiency. However, cloud resource management remains a significant challenge due to the dynamic nature of workloads, which fluctuate based on user demand, data processing requirements, and application usage patterns.

Traditional cloud resource allocation strategies rely on static policies, threshold-based rules, and manual configurations, which are often inefficient and reactive. These methods struggle to predict sudden spikes or declines in workload, leading to either resource over-provisioning (wasting computational power and increasing costs) or under-provisioning (causing performance bottlenecks and application failures). As cloud ecosystems continue to grow, more adaptive and intelligent solutions are required.

Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques have been introduced to enhance cloud resource management. These models analyze historical workload data to make predictions, but they often require frequent retraining, lack adaptability to real-time demand changes, and do not generate novel resource allocation strategies dynamically. Most ML-based solutions still rely on pre-defined models, which limits their effectiveness in handling highly volatile cloud environments.

Generative AI, particularly Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), has demonstrated significant potential in creating synthetic data, predicting future states, and simulating real-world scenarios. In the context of cloud computing, generative AI can be leveraged to simulate various workload patterns, predict resource demands, and generate optimal cloud configurations that improve performance and cost efficiency.

Additionally, reinforcement learning (RL)-based optimization has gained attention for its ability to dynamically adapt and learn from cloud workload changes. RL agents can autonomously adjust CPU, memory, and storage allocations based on real-time demand fluctuations, reducing the need for human intervention while ensuring continuous cloud performance optimization.

Despite advancements in AI-driven cloud resource management, existing solutions still lack a fully autonomous, self-optimizing framework that combines generative AI, reinforcement learning, and multi-objective optimization. Therefore, there is a strong need for a dynamic, AI-powered system that can intelligently manage cloud resources in real time, ensuring efficient cost management, energy savings, and high application availability.

OBJECTIVE OF THE INVENTION

Some of the objects of the present disclosure, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies are listed herein below.

One of the primary objectives of this invention is to develop an autonomous AI-powered framework that optimizes cloud resource allocation dynamically, without requiring manual intervention. The system should be capable of predicting workload fluctuations, adjusting resources accordingly, and minimizing costs while maintaining optimal performance.

Another objective is to integrate generative AI techniques for workload prediction and simulation, allowing the system to create synthetic resource allocation scenarios that help optimize cloud computing environments. By using GANs, VAEs, and deep learning models, the framework can continuously learn and refine cloud resource allocation strategies.

The invention also aims to incorporate reinforcement learning-based decision-making, enabling the cloud management system to self-adapt to new workload patterns in real time. By implementing Deep Q-Networks (DQN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), or similar RL algorithms, the system can continuously improve its allocation efficiency.

A further objective is to develop a multi-objective optimization layer that balances cost efficiency, energy consumption, and performance metrics. The system must ensure dynamic load balancing, power-aware computing, and real-time cloud orchestration, particularly in multi-cloud, hybrid cloud, and edge computing environments.

The invention is also designed to enhance reliability and fault tolerance by implementing a self-healing mechanism that detects resource inefficiencies, anomalies, or failures and autonomously triggers corrective actions, such as resource redistribution or predictive maintenance scheduling.

Another important goal is to ensure seamless integration with existing cloud service providers (such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud), allowing organizations to adopt AI-driven resource optimization without disrupting their existing cloud infrastructure.

Finally, the invention aims to support real-time cloud workload migration and serverless computing optimization, ensuring that serverless architectures, microservices, and containerized applications benefit from intelligent resource provisioning and improved performance scalability.

The system comprises five core components: (i) Data Aggregation Module, (ii) Generative AI Model, (iii) Reinforcement Learning Module, (iv) Multi-Objective Optimization Layer, and (v) Autonomous Decision Controller. The Data Aggregation Module continuously collects cloud performance metrics, including CPU utilization, memory load, network bandwidth, and application demand fluctuations. These data points are fed into the Generative AI Model, which generates simulated workload scenarios, predicting future cloud demands with high accuracy.

The Reinforcement Learning Module receives workload predictions and determines optimal resource allocation strategies in real-time. This module is trained using Deep Q-Networks (DQN) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithms, enabling the system to automatically adjust resource configurations based on real-time cloud demands. The Multi-Objective Optimization Layer ensures that the system balances cost-efficiency, energy consumption, and performance requirements, dynamically adjusting cloud infrastructure to prevent underutilization or overprovisioning.

The Autonomous Decision Controller acts as the execution layer of the system. Once the AI-driven resource allocation strategy is determined, the controller deploys the necessary configurations across single-cloud, multi-cloud, or hybrid cloud environments. This component is designed to work with containerized applications, such as Kubernetes-based deployments, ensuring seamless cloud orchestration. It also integrates with auto-scaling policies, serverless computing frameworks, and edge computing nodes, allowing for real-time decision-making in cloud infrastructures of varying complexities.

Additionally, the framework includes a self-healing mechanism, which continuously monitors for anomalies, inefficiencies, and potential failures in cloud resource utilization. If the system detects an irregularity, it autonomously triggers corrective actions, such as resource reallocation, load redistribution, or predictive maintenance scheduling. This ensures high availability and resilience, reducing downtime and operational costs.

The invention can be implemented in various cloud environments, including public clouds (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), private clouds, and hybrid architectures. The system is designed to seamlessly integrate with existing cloud management platforms, enabling cloud service providers and enterprises to enhance their resource efficiency, sustainability, and cost-effectiveness without manual intervention.

In one embodiment, the system is deployed in a multi-cloud infrastructure where workload demands frequently fluctuate. The Generative AI Model continuously analyzes past workload data and predicts future resource requirements using Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). The prediction results are fed into the Reinforcement Learning Module, which dynamically adjusts CPU, memory, and storage allocations across different cloud providers.

For instance, if a sudden spike in traffic is predicted for a cloud-hosted e-commerce platform, the system proactively allocates additional virtual machines (VMs) or increases containerized application instances. Once the demand decreases, the system automatically scales down resources, ensuring cost-efficient cloud usage. This embodiment prevents resource wastage and under-provisioning, enhancing cloud performance.

This embodiment focuses on minimizing cloud operational costs and energy consumption while maintaining high-performance levels. The Reinforcement Learning Module continuously learns from historical billing data and cloud power consumption patterns, optimizing the cost-energy tradeoff for cloud resource allocations.

For example, in a data-intensive AI training workload, the system determines optimal GPU allocations based on both performance needs and energy consumption trends. If cheaper, energy-efficient computing instances are available, the system migrates workloads to those instances, reducing costs. Additionally, the system integrates with renewable energy-aware cloud data centers, shifting computational workloads to regions with lower carbon footprints, making cloud operations more sustainable.

In yet another embodiment, the system is applied to edge computing environments, where cloud services are distributed across geographically dispersed edge nodes. The Decision Controller dynamically orchestrates workloads between centralized cloud data centers and edge nodes, ensuring low-latency service delivery.

For example, in an autonomous vehicle network, the system monitors real-time sensor data processing requirements. If high-latency cloud interactions could disrupt vehicle operations, the system prioritizes computing at edge nodes (e.g., in-vehicle processors). However, for computationally heavy tasks like AI-based traffic pattern prediction, workloads are offloaded to cloud GPUs dynamically.

Similarly, for serverless computing environments, the system optimizes function execution times, ensuring cost-efficient and performance-driven resource allocation. It automatically adjusts serverless instance provisioning based on historical request patterns, reducing cold starts and optimizing execution latency.

Description:The present invention relates to the field of consumer analytics, particularly to a system and device that utilize artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and real-time data collection techniques to predict consumer behavior patterns, preferences, and decision-making tendencies. The invention aims to enhance personalized marketing, optimize inventory management, and improve consumer engagement strategies by leveraging multi-source data analytics in retail and e-commerce environments.

Consumer behavior analysis has been a cornerstone of market research, enabling businesses to tailor their offerings and marketing strategies to meet customer preferences. Traditional methods, such as surveys and purchase history analysis, rely heavily on past data, which often fails to capture real-time behavioral shifts. These conventional techniques are time-consuming and lack the agility to provide immediate, actionable insights.

The rise of digital technologies has introduced new methods of consumer behavior tracking, including website analytics, recommendation engines, and loyalty programs. However, these approaches are often limited to online interactions, missing crucial offline consumer behaviors such as in-store browsing patterns, physical product interactions, and real-time decision-making cues. This gap restricts the ability of businesses to make comprehensive consumer behavior predictions.

Advancements in artificial intelligence and machine learning have provided a promising avenue for improving consumer behavior predictions. By leveraging AI-driven algorithms, businesses can analyze vast amounts of structured and unstructured data to derive insights into customer preferences, habits, and purchasing triggers. Despite these advancements, current AI-based solutions often struggle with integrating multi-source real-time data, leading to inaccuracies and delayed responses in consumer analytics.

Additionally, consumer behavior is influenced by multiple external factors such as socio-economic trends, cultural influences, seasonal demands, and personal emotions. Existing prediction models do not account for these dynamic factors effectively, resulting in generalized recommendations that lack personalized precision. A robust solution must incorporate contextual data, enabling adaptive predictions that evolve based on real-time inputs.

Another critical challenge in consumer behavior prediction is data privacy and security. With the growing concern over consumer data protection regulations, businesses must ensure that data collection and analysis methods comply with industry standards while maintaining high prediction accuracy. Many existing solutions rely on centralized databases that pose risks of data breaches and unauthorized access.

To address these limitations, there is a need for a Consumer Behavior Prediction Device that integrates real-time data from multiple sources, applies advanced AI-driven analytics, and provides businesses with adaptive, privacy-compliant, and actionable consumer insights. The proposed invention aims to bridge the gap between traditional consumer research and modern AI-powered behavior prediction methodologies.

OBJECTIVE OF THE INVENTION

Some of the objects of the present disclosure, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies are listed herein below.

One objective of the invention is to develop an advanced Consumer Behavior Prediction Device that utilizes real-time data collection through IoT sensors, smart cameras, and wearable technologies to enhance the accuracy of behavioral predictions. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on past purchase data, the proposed device dynamically monitors consumer interactions in both online and offline environments.

Another objective of the invention is to implement AI-driven predictive analytics that continuously learn from consumer actions and preferences. By employing deep learning models, the system refines its predictions over time, ensuring businesses receive up-to-date insights into changing consumer trends and behaviors.

A further objective is to design a multi-source data integration framework that collects, processes, and analyzes data from diverse inputs such as product interactions, biometric signals, social media activity, and historical purchasing patterns. This holistic approach allows businesses to gain a deeper understanding of customer decision-making processes.

Additionally, the invention aims to provide real-time recommendations for businesses, enabling them to optimize marketing campaigns, personalize product offerings, and adjust pricing strategies based on predicted consumer preferences. By integrating with retail management systems, the device ensures seamless execution of targeted consumer engagement strategies.

Another key objective is to ensure data security and privacy compliance by implementing decentralized processing architectures and encryption mechanisms. This prevents unauthorized access to consumer data while ensuring businesses remain compliant with global data protection regulations such as GDPR and CCPA.

The invention also seeks to support cross-industry applications, making it adaptable to retail, e-commerce, hospitality, and service-based industries. Whether used in brick-and-mortar stores or online platforms, the device provides valuable insights that improve customer experiences and business outcomes.

Finally, an essential objective is to enhance consumer engagement and satisfaction by creating personalized shopping experiences. By predicting consumer needs before they arise, businesses can proactively offer recommendations, discounts, and services tailored to individual preferences, ultimately increasing customer loyalty and revenue growth.

The communication interface seamlessly integrates with external retail management, e-commerce, and customer relationship management (CRM) platforms, enabling businesses to execute personalized marketing strategies efficiently. The present invention provides a Consumer Behavior Prediction Device that integrates real-time data collection with AI-driven predictive analytics to generate accurate insights into consumer decision-making. The device comprises multiple hardware and software components, including IoT-based sensors, a central AI processing unit, a prediction engine, and a communication interface for seamless integration with external business systems.

The data collection module utilizes various sensors, including RFID tags, NFC readers, infrared motion detectors, smart cameras, and biometric sensors. These components enable the system to capture real-time consumer interactions in retail stores, online platforms, or service-based environments. The collected data includes parameters such as product engagement, gaze tracking, movement patterns, purchase frequency, and emotional responses derived from facial recognition technology.

The AI processing unit employs deep learning algorithms, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for image recognition, recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for sequential behavior analysis, and reinforcement learning models for adaptive behavior prediction. The AI system continuously refines its prediction accuracy by incorporating both historical and real-time consumer data. It also utilizes sentiment analysis and natural language processing (NLP) techniques to analyze textual and verbal feedback from customers.

The prediction engine processes the analyzed data to generate insights on consumer preferences, potential purchasing decisions, and personalized product recommendations. It evaluates multiple behavioral indicators, such as time spent on a product, frequency of engagement, comparison tendencies, and social influence factors, to assess purchase probability. The system further applies clustering algorithms to segment consumers into distinct behavioral profiles, allowing businesses to optimize targeted marketing campaigns.

The communication interface enables seamless integration with external platforms such as customer relationship management (CRM) systems, e-commerce platforms, and retail management software. The device can transmit real-time alerts, generate personalized promotional offers, and update inventory management systems based on predicted demand fluctuations. Additionally, businesses can access predictive insights via a cloud-based dashboard or an API for real-time data synchronization.

To ensure data privacy and security, the system employs decentralized edge computing techniques, encrypted data storage, and privacy-preserving AI models. The device follows regulatory compliance standards such as GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) and CCPA (California Consumer Privacy Act) to protect consumer data while providing businesses with actionable intelligence. The modular design of the device makes it adaptable for various industries, including retail, e-commerce, hospitality, and entertainment.

In one embodiment, the Consumer Behavior Prediction Device is deployed in a physical retail store to monitor consumer interactions with products in real-time. The device is equipped with smart cameras and RFID sensors embedded in product shelves to track consumer engagement with specific items.

When a consumer picks up a product, the RFID tag sends data to the AI processing unit, which analyzes how long the consumer holds the product, whether they compare it with other items, and whether they place it back on the shelf or proceed to checkout. The AI system assesses this behavioral data alongside historical purchase patterns and external factors such as ongoing promotions or store layout adjustments.

The prediction engine then determines the likelihood of a purchase and, if necessary, triggers an automated recommendation via an in-store digital screen or a mobile app notification. For example, if a consumer spends significant time browsing a specific product but does not make a purchase, the system may offer a discount coupon in real time to encourage conversion.

The system can also update inventory predictions based on consumer engagement, allowing retailers to optimize stock levels dynamically. The in-store behavior prediction system helps businesses improve customer experience, enhance sales strategies, and minimize inventory losses.

In another embodiment, the Consumer Behavior Prediction Device is integrated into an e-commerce platform to analyze online consumer interactions. The system captures real-time browsing behaviors, such as click patterns, time spent on product pages, shopping cart activities, and search queries.

The AI processing unit employs deep learning algorithms to analyze user preferences based on previous purchases, product reviews, and browsing habits. It also integrates sentiment analysis techniques to assess consumer emotions from product reviews, chatbot interactions, and customer feedback messages.

If the system detects hesitation behavior, such as adding items to the cart but not proceeding to checkout, the prediction engine calculates the probability of purchase abandonment. In response, the system can trigger automated engagement mechanisms, such as sending a personalized email reminder, offering a limited-time discount, or suggesting complementary products.

Additionally, the device integrates with recommendation engines, dynamically adjusting product suggestions based on real-time user behavior. This embodiment improves user engagement, enhances conversion rates, and optimizes e-commerce marketing strategies.

In another embodiment, the Consumer Behavior Prediction Device is implemented as a wearable AI system that tracks physiological and emotional responses to shopping experiences. This wearable device, such as smart glasses, wristbands, or biometric rings, collects heart rate variability, galvanic skin response, and facial expressions to gauge consumer sentiment during product interactions.

For example, if a consumer enters a store wearing smart glasses integrated with the system, the device records their gaze duration on products, pupil dilation (indicating interest), and facial expressions (indicating emotional responses). The AI processing unit processes this data in real-time and correlates physiological reactions with potential purchasing intent.

The prediction engine generates insights, such as identifying which product categories evoke the highest positive engagement, allowing retailers to optimize in-store product placement. Additionally, the wearable device can provide real-time product recommendations via augmented reality (AR) overlays, guiding consumers to personalized shopping experiences.

This embodiment is particularly useful for luxury brands, high-end fashion stores, and experiential retail environments, where consumer emotions significantly influence purchasing decisions. The wearable AI system enhances customer engagement while providing businesses with advanced sentiment-driven insights.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

The digital revolution has transformed consumer behavior, leading to an exponential increase in data generation across various digital platforms, including e-commerce, social media, search engines, and online reviews. Businesses are now leveraging this data to gain insights into consumer preferences, purchasing habits, and decision-making patterns. However, traditional analytical approaches often fail to process and interpret such vast datasets effectively.

The emergence of big data analytics has introduced scalable and intelligent mechanisms for handling complex and high-volume consumer data. By incorporating machine learning algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI), and predictive modeling, businesses can now extract meaningful patterns, detect trends, and forecast consumer needs with greater accuracy.

Despite the availability of data-driven technologies, several challenges exist in consumer behavior prediction. These include data heterogeneity, noise filtering, real-time processing, and privacy concerns. Conventional models often struggle to integrate diverse data sources while maintaining accuracy and efficiency in predictions.

Additionally, real-time consumer behavior analysis requires advanced infrastructure capable of processing structured (transactional data) and unstructured (social media interactions, reviews, multimedia content) data simultaneously. Existing solutions lack an efficient mechanism for real-time insights generation, which is critical for personalized recommendations and targeted marketing campaigns.

Another significant limitation is the inability to dynamically adapt to evolving consumer preferences. Abstract:
Abstract:

The present disclosure provides a method for fabricating hemophobic and antibacterial surfaces on Ti6Al4V biomedical implants to enhance hemocompatibility and infection resistance. The method involves sputtering a metal catalyst layer (Cu, Ag, Ti, Zn) onto the Ti6Al4V substrate, followed by carbon nanofiber (CNF) deposition using chemical vapor deposition (CVD) at 320°C. The surface is then annealed to improve durability. The resulting CNF-coated Ti6Al4V exhibits superhydrophobicity, with water and blood contact angles exceeding 130°, reducing platelet activation, hemolysis, and clot formation. Antibacterial assessments demonstrate a 58% reduction in E. coli viability compared to bare Ti6Al4V surfaces. The invention is scalable, biocompatible, and ideal for LVADs and other blood-contacting implants, minimizing device-associated infections and thrombogenic risks. This novel modification significantly improves the longevity and safety of biomedical implants, addressing a critical need in cardiovascular medicine.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION
[0001] The present disclosure relates to the field of biomedical engineering, specifically to the modification of metal surfaces to enhance their hemocompatibility and antibacterial properties. The invention is particularly applicable to medical devices such as Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs), cardiovascular implants, and other blood-contacting biomedical components, where surface modification is essential to prevent thrombosis, infection, and other complications.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[0002] Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art. 
[0003] Metals and alloys have been extensively used in biomedical implants and blood-contacting medical devices due to their excellent biocompatibility, mechanical strength, and corrosion resistance. However, a major drawback of metal surfaces is their inherent hemoincompatibility, which can lead to thrombosis, hemolysis, and excessive protein adsorption, increasing the risk of device failure and postoperative complications. Furthermore, biomedical implants and assistive devices often serve as a breeding ground for bacterial colonization, leading to device-associated infections that can result in severe complications, extended hospital stays, and high morbidity and mortality rates.
[0004] Existing surface modification techniques, such as surface texturing, polymer coatings, and drug-eluting layers, have attempted to improve hemocompatibility and antibacterial efficacy. However, these methods suffer from limited long-term stability, poor adhesion to metallic surfaces, and the potential for degradation in biological environments. In particular, polymeric and hydrophilic coatings tend to deteriorate over time, losing their protective properties, while antibiotic-based coatings contribute to the rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), posing significant challenges in clinical settings.
[0005] Additionally, conventional plasma treatments and chemical etching processes used to improve surface hydrophobicity have demonstrated limited success in achieving sustained hemophobicity in blood-contacting applications. The challenge remains to develop a scalable, durable, and multifunctional surface modification technique that can effectively address both thrombogenicity and bacterial colonization without compromising the mechanical integrity and biocompatibility of the underlying Ti6Al4V substrate.
[0006] With the increasing global burden of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) and the rising demand for long-term implantable medical devices, the need for an innovative surface engineering approach is more critical than ever. A robust and scalable method that enables the development of superhydrophobic, hemophobic, and antibacterial surfaces on metals could significantly enhance the efficacy, safety, and lifespan of medical implants, reducing complications and improving patient outcomes.

OBJECTIVE OF THE INVENTION
[0007] The primary objective of the invention is to develop a hemophobic and antibacterial surface on Ti6Al4V-based biomedical implants, particularly for Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs) and other blood-contacting medical components. 
[0008] Another objective of the present disclosure is to develop a superhydrophobic and hemophobic Ti6Al4V surface that prevents thrombosis, protein adsorption, and clot formation in blood-contacting medical devices.
[0009] Another objective of the present disclosure is to integrate carbon nanofibers (CNFs) as a surface coating through a controlled and reproducible process, ensuring high durability and mechanical strength.
[0010] Another objective of the present disclosure is to introduce metal catalyst coatings (Cu, Ag, Ti, Zn) on Ti6Al4V using sputtering technology, enabling the efficient growth of CNFs through chemical vapor deposition (CVD).
[0011] Another objective of the present disclosure is to optimize the CVD process for controlled CNF deposition by regulating gas flow rates, deposition times, and temperature conditions, ensuring uniform and defect-free coatings.
[0012] Another objective of the present disclosure is to validate the hemophobicity of the developed surface by measuring the contact angle with water and human blood, ensuring a contact angle above 130°.
[0013] Another objective of the present disclosure is to demonstrate antibacterial properties of the CNF-coated Ti6Al4V surfaces against Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), preventing implant-related infections.
[0014] Another objective of the present disclosure is to enhance long-term stability by incorporating annealing techniques that improve coating adhesion, mechanical strength, and durability in biological environments.
[0015] Another objective of the present disclosure is to ensure compatibility with existing medical devices, particularly in cardiovascular implants, enabling seamless integration into commercial LVADs and other assistive circulatory devices.
[0016] Another objective of the present disclosure is to provide a scalable, cost-effective, and reproducible process for mass production, ensuring the widespread clinical adoption of the technology.
[0017] Another objective of the present disclosure is to improve patient safety and outcomes by reducing post-implantation complications, infection rates, and thrombosis-associated risks, leading to better long-term prognosis and device efficiency.
[0018] Another objective of the present disclosure is to address the challenges of thrombosis, hemolysis, bacterial colonization, and poor long-term stability of existing coatings.

SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
[0019] The present disclosure generally relates to a novel method for fabricating superhydrophobic, hemophobic, and antibacterial surfaces on Ti6Al4V-based biomedical implants, particularly for Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs) and other blood-contacting medical components. The method involves sputtering a metal catalyst layer (Cu, Ag, Ti, or Zn) onto a Ti6Al4V substrate, followed by the growth of carbon nanofibers (CNFs) using a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) process at a controlled temperature of 320°C in a hydrogen gas environment. After deposition, the surface undergoes annealing to enhance coating adhesion and mechanical strength, ensuring long-term durability in biological environments. 
[0020] In an aspect, the resulting CNF-coated Ti6Al4V surface exhibits superhydrophobic properties, with contact angles exceeding 130° for water and human blood, effectively reducing platelet activation, hemolysis, and thrombosis formation. Furthermore, the coating demonstrates significant antibacterial efficacy, inhibiting the growth of Escherichia coli (E. coli) and Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) by more than 50% compared to non-coated surfaces. 
[0021] In an aspect, this scalable, cost-effective, and reproducible surface modification technique provides a highly durable, biocompatible, and infection-resistant solution for blood-contacting medical implants, reducing the risk of device-related complications and improving patient outcomes. 
[0022] In an aspect, the present disclosure provides a hemophobic and antibacterial surface comprising: 
 a substrate coated with at least one metal catalyst; and
 a layer grown on the metal catalyst-coated substrate.
[0023] In an aspect,  the present disclosure provides a method for fabricating a hemophobic and antibacterial surface on a Ti6Al4V substrate, comprising the steps of:
coating the substrate with at least one metal catalyst using a sputtering process in an inert gas atmosphere
placing the metal-coated substrate in a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) chamber under a hydrogen gas environment during heating period from the temperature 25 ºC to 250 - 350°C. 
introducing acetylene gas into the CVD chamber for a period of up to 15 to 40 minutes at a constant temperature ranging from 250 – 350 ºC, to facilitate the growth of carbon nanofibers (CNFs) on the metal-coated Ti6Al4V substrate followed by cooling the chamber to room temperature under a nitrogen gas environment to stabilize the CNF-coated surface; and
annealing the coated surface to enhance coating strength, durability, and adhesion.

[0057] The present disclosure provides a method for fabricating superhydrophobic, hemophobic, and antibacterial surfaces on Ti6Al4V biomedical implants, particularly for Left Ventricular Assist Devices (LVADs) and other blood-contacting medical devices. The coated substrate is then subjected to a chemical vapor deposition (CVD) process at 320°C in a hydrogen gas atmosphere, where acetylene gas is introduced for 15–20 minutes to enable the deposition of CNFs.
