Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to a modular mobility assistive device for strollers that is capable of providing a means that is affixed on back portion of a stroller for allowing a user to maneuver the stroller with ease while standing on the means, thus offering a more comfortable and efficient way to navigate both smooth and uneven surfaces.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002] In conventional stroller, users typically need to push the stroller manually, which can become strenuous, especially over long distances or on uneven terrain. Additionally, there are no integrated mechanisms in these systems to assist users who may have mobility challenges or require a platform to stand while maneuvering the stroller. As a result, traditional strollers lack the necessary features to provide added comfort and ease of use for both the user and the person in the stroller, particularly in situations where both convenience and stability are required.

[0003] Existing solutions for enhancing stroller mobility are often limited to passive mechanisms like wheels or handles, without providing active assistance in movement or surface adaptation. Furthermore, current designs do not offer advanced control features, such as voice-activated movement, nor do they address issues related to stability when moving over uneven surfaces. Therefore, there is a need for a more versatile, stable, and user-friendly mobility assistive device that can work in conjunction with strollers to improve both mobility and comfort for users, while integrating advanced control features for enhanced ease of use. 

[0004] US20220212706A1 discloses about a motorized stroller assembly includes a carriage frame. A plurality of wheels is rotatably attached to the carriage and a child seat is positioned in the carriage frame. An electric motor is mechanically coupled to at least a first wheel of the plurality of wheels. The motor selectively rotates the first wheel to drive the carriage frame forward. A battery is mounted on the carriage frame and is electrically coupled to the motor. A control is mounted on the carriage frame and is electrically coupled to the motor and is actuated to drive the first wheel in the first direction. A platform is attached to a rear side of the carriage and extends rearwardly therefrom. The platform is positioned near a bottom of the carriage. The platform supports a person standing on the platform. A canopy is pivotally coupled to the carriage frame and is extendable over the child seat. Although, US’706 provides a stroller assembly featuring a platform extending rearward from the carriage frame to support a person standing on it, however the device fails to provide a means for stabilizing the platform based on surface variations, which may result in instability when used on uneven terrain.

[0005] GB2484825A discloses about a child stroller and a stand platform assembly thereof are disclosed. The stroller includes a frame 12, a brake assembly 14 connected to the frame, two rear wheels 16 connected to the brake assembly, and the stand platform assembly 18 for carrying a child in a standing position. The stand platform assembly includes a platform (182, figure 6) connected to a rear cross bar of the frame, and two sidewalls (184) connected to two opposite sides of the platform. When the stroller is folded, said stroller is capable of being supported upright by the sidewalls and the rear wheels (figure 7), which solves the inconvenience in placing a folded conventional stroller. The platform is capable of being pivoted upwards when one of the sidewalls hits an object, thus preventing it from being damaged. Although, GB’825 discloses a child stroller and a stand platform assembly, however the device fails to provide a means for stabilizing the platform over uneven terrain, which is critical for ensuring the safety and comfort of the user.
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed for providing mobility assistance with strollers, however, these devices fail to in providing features such as automatic stabilization when navigating uneven surfaces, multi-axis movement for enhanced maneuverability.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that provide a means for stabilizing the platform over varying terrains, enables multi-directional movement, and provides an intuitive control mechanism for seamless interaction between the user and the device.

[0009]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that provide a means that is affixed on back portion of a stroller for allowing a user to maneuver the stroller with ease while standing on the means, thus offering a more comfortable and efficient way to navigate both smooth and uneven surfaces.

[0010] Another object of the present invention is to develop a device that detects rotational speed and direction of the stroller’s wheels, and accordingly regulates actuation of the wheels for facilitating smooth motion of platform with respect to the stroller.

[0022] The proposed device herein comprises of a rectangular platform 101 developed to be positioned at back portion of a stroller, wherein the platform 101 is accessed by a user maneuvering the stroller for attaining a standing posture over the platform 101. The platform 101 is made up of material not restricted to wood, metal etc. that provides durability to the components and comfortably accommodate all the components required to perform the specified operation.

[0023] A user is required to press a push button integrated with the device, such that when the user presses the push button, it initiates an electrical circuit mechanism. Inside the push button, there is a spring-loaded contact mechanism that, under normal circumstances, maintains an open circuit. When the button is pressed, it compresses the spring, causing the contacts to meet and complete the circuit. This closure then sends an electrical signal to an inbuilt microcontroller associated with the device to either power up or shut down. Conversely, releasing the button allows the spring to return to its original position, breaking the circuit and sending the signal to deactivate the device. 

[0024] On activation of the device, the microcontroller activates a pair of motorized clamping units 102 attached with the platform 101 for acquiring a grip at the back portion of the stroller. The motorized clamping unit 102 are powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller by providing required electric current to the motor. The motor comprises of a coil that converts the received electric current into mechanical force by generating magnetic field, thus the mechanical force provides the required power to the clamping unit 102 thus extending/retracting for clasping back portion of the stroller.

[0025] A laser-based sensor 104 is installed over the platform 101 to determine level of the ground surface. The laser-based sensor 104 comprises two main components: a laser diode that emits the laser beam, a photodiode that detects the reflected light. When the sensor 104 is activated as commanded by the microcontroller, the laser diode emits a short pulse of laser light towards the ground surface. The light reflects off the surface and returns to the sensor 104. The photodiode then detects this reflected light. By precisely measuring the time it takes for the laser pulse to travel to the target and back, the sensor 104 calculates the distance. The pattern of the received pulse gets converted into an analog value which is further converted into an electrical signal, wherein the electrical signal is send to the microcontroller. The microcontroller then processes the received signal from the sensor 104, thus determining level of the ground surface. 

[0026] As per the determined level of the ground surface, the microcontroller activates a hydraulically operated rod attached in between each of the wheels 103 and platform 101 to stabilize the platform 101 over the surface. The hydraulically operated rod is powered by a hydraulic unit consisting of a hydraulic cylinder, hydraulic compressor, hydraulic valve and piston that work in collaboration for providing the required extension/retraction to the rod. Such that the microcontroller actuates the valve to allow passage of hydraulic fluid from the compressor within the cylinder, the hydraulic fluid further develops pressure against the piston and results in pushing and extending the piston. The piston is connected with the rod and due to applied pressure the rod extends and similarly, the microcontroller retracts the rod by closing the valve resulting in retraction of the piston. The microcontroller regulates the extension/retraction of the rod for stabilizing the platform 101 over the surface.

[0027] The user access a microphone 105 configured on the platform 101 for providing voice commands regarding maneuvering the platform 101 with the stroller. The microphone 105 consists of a diaphragm, typically made of a thin, flexible material such as metal or plastic. When sound waves reach the microphone 105, they cause the diaphragm to vibrate. These vibrations are directly proportional to the variations in air pressure caused by the sound waves. The diaphragm is coupled to a coil of wire, as the diaphragm vibrates, the coil moves within a magnetic field, inducing an electric current in the wire. This current is proportional to the amplitude and frequency of the sound waves. The electrical signal generated by the diaphragm-coil is transmitted to the microcontroller. 

[0028] The microcontroller on receiving the signals actuates multiple motorized wheels 103 arranged underneath the platform 101 to maneuver the platform 101 over a ground surface. The wheels 103 are powered by are powered by a DC (Direct Current) motor, which convert electrical energy into mechanical motion. When the platform 101 receives electric current from an external source, the DC motors generate rotational force. This force is then transmitted to the wheels 103 via a gearbox, which converts the rotary motion into linear motion, propelling the platform 101 forward, backward, or sideways as required. The motorized omnidirectional wheels 103 are designed to move independently, allowing the platform 101 to change direction smoothly and precisely by adjusting the speed and direction of each wheels 103 individually.

[0029] A motorized ball and socket joint is integrated in between the clamping unit 102 and platform 101 that is actuated by the microcontroller for providing multi-axis rotational motion to the platform 101. The ball and socket joint provides a 360-degree rotation to the platform 101 for aiding the platform 101 to turn at a desired angle. The ball and socket joint is a coupling consisting of a ball joint securely locked within a socket joint, where the ball joint is able to move in a 360-degree rotation within the socket thus, providing the required rotational motion to the platform 101. The ball and socket joint is powered by a DC (direct current) motor that is actuated by the microcontroller thus providing multidirectional movement to the platform 101 for facilitating precise and smooth movement of the platform 101 with the stroller.

[0030] Further, an incremental encoder sensor 106 is attached with the platform 101 for detection rotational speed and direction of the wheels 103. The incremental encoder sensor 106 works by converting the rotational motion of the wheels 103 into electrical signals to measure speed and direction. The incremental encoder sensor 106 consists of a rotating disc with evenly spaced markings or slots, an LED or light source, and a photodetector. As the disc rotates with the wheels 103, the light source emits a beam that passes through the slots on the disc. The photodetector senses the interruptions in the light beam caused by the rotating disc and generates pulses corresponding to the rotation. The frequency of these pulses determines the rotational speed, while the phase difference between two channels of pulses allows the detection of the direction of rotation. The microcontroller receives these pulses and processes the speed and direction data, adjusting the motor's actuation to ensure smooth movement of the platform 101 with respect to the stroller.

[0031] The device is associated with a battery for providing the required power to the electronically and electrically operated components including the microcontroller, electrically powered sensors, motorized components and alike of the device. The battery within the device is preferably a lithium-ion-battery which is a rechargeable battery and recharges by deriving the required power from an external power source. The derived power is further stored in form of chemical energy within the battery, which when required by the components of the device derive the required energy in the form of electric current for ensuring smooth and proper functioning of the device.

Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates to a modular child seating assistive device for bicycles that is capable of providing a means to comfortably accommodate a child on a bicycle.

BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
 
[0002]  Assistive seating devices for children while riding bicycles are designed to enhance safety and comfort for young riders who may have physical or developmental challenges. These devices, which often include specially designed seats or harnesses, provide additional support and stability, ensuring that children with motor impairments or coordination issues can ride more securely. They are typically adjustable to accommodate various sizes and needs, and are engineered to fit standard bicycle frames or be mounted onto adaptive bikes. Such seating devices often feature safety straps, high backrests, and padded cushioning to prevent falls and reduce the risk of injury. By offering tailored support, these assistive devices enable children with diverse needs to enjoy cycling, fostering independence and inclusion in recreational activities.

[0003]  Traditional methods for providing assistance to children while riding bicycles typically involve using standard child seats or bike trailers that attach to the rear of the bike. These seats are designed to secure the child with harnesses and provide some support, but they may not always address the specific needs of children with physical or developmental challenges. Issues with these traditional methods include limited adjustability, which can make it difficult to accommodate children with varying levels of support needs or physical sizes. Additionally, standard seats may not offer adequate back or lateral support, potentially leading to discomfort or safety concerns. The design of these seats may also impact the child's ability to engage fully with the biking experience, affecting both safety and enjoyment.

[0004] US8251388B2 discloses a bicycle child seat. The bicycle child seat may include a seat sized for a child, a safety harness configured to secure the child in the bicycle child seat, a bicycle frame attachment mechanism, and a seat post attachment mechanism. The seat may include a hole configured to slide over the seat post of the bicycle. Though US’388 relates to a bicycle child seat, however, the cited art lacks in monitoring angle of a child’s body with respect to a bicycle to prevent falling of the child.

[0005] CA2435242A1 discloses a bike tutor is a device designed for the purpose of teaching children the balance and feel of riding a bicycle. The bike tutor comprises of a seat and foot rests, mounted to the head tube of an adult sized bicycle. The bike tutor does not make contact to any other section of the bicycle. The bike tutor assembly is located between the seat and handlebars of the bicycle. The child occupant hands grasp the handlebars of the bicycle between the adult operators hand position on the bicycle. The bike tutor is designed to keep interference with the adults handling of the bicycle to a minimum. The bike tutors foot rests fold upward when not in use. Though CA’242 relates to a bike tutor, however, the cited art lacks in providing a means to absorb jerk or shocks experienced by a user.
 
[0006] Conventionally, many devices have been developed to provide assistance to children in sitting while riding a bicycle, however, the prior arts mentioned above have limitations pertaining to monitor angle of a child’s body with respect to a bicycle to prevent falling of the child and in providing a means to absorb jerk or shocks experienced by a user.

[0007] In order to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks, there exists a need in the art to develop a device that is capable of monitoring angle of a child’s body with respect to a bicycle and accordingly adjust to form a boundary around the child, thereby preventing the child from falling off the bicycle and providing a means to absorb jerk or shocks experienced by a user during motion of a bicycle.

[0008]  The principal object of the present invention is to overcome the disadvantages of the prior art.

[0009]  An object of the present invention is to develop a device that is capable of providing a means to comfortably accommodate a child on a bicycle as per user requirement.

Abstract:
Abstract:

The present disclosure proposes a method for enhancing the properties of recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) by integrating chemical and physical treatments to improve its strength, density, durability, and compatibility with cementitious matrices. The method improves the mechanical properties of the RCA, such as aggregate crushing value (ACV), aggregate impact value (AIV), and bulk density, making it comparable to natural aggregates. The method enhances the interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between the RCA and cement paste, thereby ensuring better bonding and higher structural integrity in concrete applications. The method is scalable and cost-effective, which allows for industrial-scale RCA processing without excessive energy consumption or high operational costs. The method reduces the water absorption of the RCA by efficiently removing or modifying residual mortar through a combination of chemical and physical treatments.

Field of the invention:
[0001] The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of civil engineering and sustainable construction materials, in specific, relates to a method for enhancing the properties of recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) by integrating chemical and physical treatments to improve its strength, density, durability, and compatibility with cementitious matrices.
Background of the invention:
[0002] The global construction industry is experiencing rapid growth, leading to an increased demand for natural aggregates, which are essential components of concrete. However, the over-extraction of these aggregates has raised serious environmental concerns, including depletion of natural resources, habitat destruction, and increased carbon emissions. As a result, there has been a strong push towards the utilization of recycled materials, particularly recycled concrete aggregate (RCA), as a sustainable alternative to natural aggregates.

[0003] While RCA presents an eco-friendly and cost-effective solution for the industry, its widespread adoption is hindered by several limitations. One of the primary challenges is the presence of residual mortar on RCA particles, which increases porosity and water absorption, and weakens interfacial bonding with cement paste. This residual mortar negatively impacts the mechanical performance and durability of RCA-based concrete, making it inferior to conventional natural aggregates.

[0004] Various techniques have been explored to enhance the properties of RCA. Mechanical methods, such as crushing and grinding, aim to remove residual mortar and improve particle shape, but they often lead to excessive fines and micro-cracks, which further compromise the aggregate’s structural integrity. Thermal treatment is another approach, where RCA is subjected to high temperatures to weaken and detach the adhered mortar. However, this process requires high energy consumption and may induce additional micro-cracking, reducing the overall strength of the material.

[0005] Chemical treatments using acids, alkalis, and other reagents have been employed to dissolve residual mortar and modify RCA surface properties. While effective in reducing porosity and enhancing aggregate bonding, these methods often suffer from slow reaction rates, uneven treatment distribution, and environmental concerns due to chemical waste generation. Additionally, the individual application of chemical or physical treatments has yielded inconsistent results, as each method alone fails to comprehensively address all RCA deficiencies.

[0006] Despite these challenges, recent advancements in materials science and engineering have opened new possibilities for synergistic treatment approaches. By combining multiple treatment techniques, it may be possible to overcome the individual shortcomings of existing methods and develop a more effective and scalable solution for RCA enhancement. However, existing research has yet to fully explore the integration of complementary chemical and physical processes that can collectively optimize RCA properties for industrial applications.

[0007] Moreover, industrial scalability remains a significant concern. Many of the advanced RCA treatment techniques proposed in research settings are not practical for large-scale implementation, either due to high operational costs, complex processing requirements, or environmental constraints. The need for a cost-efficient, environmentally friendly, and high-performance solution to improve RCA properties is critical for the wider adoption of sustainable construction practices.

[0008] By addressing all the above-mentioned problems, there is a need for a method for enhancing the properties of recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) by integrating chemical and physical treatments to improve its strength, density, durability, and compatibility with cementitious matrices. There is also a need for a method for reducing the water absorption of RCA by efficiently removing or modifying residual mortar through a combination of chemical and physical treatments. There is also a need for a method that improves the mechanical properties of RCA, such as aggregate crushing value (ACV), aggregate impact value (AIV), and bulk density, making it comparable to natural aggregates.

[0009] Additionally, there is also a need for a method that enhances the interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between RCA and cement paste, thereby ensuring better bonding and higher structural integrity in concrete applications. There is also a need for a method that is scalable and cost-effective, which allows for industrial-scale RCA processing without excessive energy consumption or high operational costs. There is also a need for an environmentally friendly method that minimizes chemical waste and optimizes resource utilization, thereby contributing to sustainable construction practices. There is also a need for a method that allows for sequential or simultaneous application of chemical and physical treatments, thereby offering flexibility based on the contamination level of RCA. Further, there is also a need for a method that provides a sustainable and high-performance solution for construction and demolition waste recycling, thereby aligning with global environmental regulations and green building initiatives.

[0022] According to another aspect, the invention provides a method for a flowchart of a method for enhancing the properties of the RCA. At one step, the RCA is immersed in a citric acid solution at a concentration of at least 1% to 10% to dissolve residual mortar, thereby obtaining an acid-treated RCA. In one embodiment herein, the citric acid immersion is conducted at a temperature between 25°C and 60°C to reaction kinetics while preserving the RCA structural integrity.

[0023] At another step, the acid-treated RCA is subjected to vibratory milling at a frequency range of at least 10 Hz to 50 Hz and an impact force of at least 50 N to 500 N for a time period of 10 to 120 min to refine particle morphology, eliminate micro-cracks, and enhance surface texture, thereby obtaining a milled RCA. In one embodiment herein, the vibratory milling intensity is adjusted based on the level of contamination and aggregate size distribution to maximize surface refinement.

[0024] At another step, the milled RCA is treated with a sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution at a concentration of at least 1% to 8%, optionally combined with ultrasonic cavitation, to detach residual mortar and enhance surface densification, thereby obtaining NaOH-treated RCA. In one embodiment herein, the ultrasonic cavitation is applied during the NaOH treatment at a frequency of at least 20 kHz to 40 kHz to enhance mortar detachment efficiency, thereby leading to improved bonding characteristics in cementitious applications.

[0025] At another step, the NaOH-treated RCA is rinsed to remove chemical residues, thereby performing post-treatment drying at a controlled temperature. In one embodiment herein, the NaOH treatment is conducted for a time period of at least 30 min to 4 hr depending on the contamination level and surface composition of the RCA. In one embodiment herein, the post-treatment drying is conducted at an ambient temperature of at least 120°C to achieve optimal moisture reduction while preserving the RCA structural integrity.

[0026] Further, at other step, the NaOH-treated RCA is heated by applying controlled thermal cycling at a temperature of at least 100°C to 200°C for a time period of at least 30 min to 3 hr, followed by cooling, to reduce porosity and improve aggregate toughness, thereby obtaining an enhanced RCA with reduced water absorption, increased density, and improved compatibility with cementitious matrices. In one embodiment herein, the thermal cycling process involves gradual cooling using air, water, or liquid nitrogen to prevent thermal shock and microstructural damage. In one embodiment herein, the enhanced RCA exhibits a water absorption reduction from 5-10% to 1.5-4.5% and an increase in bulk density from 1200-1500 kg/m³ to 1500-1800 kg/m³.

[0027] In one embodiment herein, the treated RCA achieves an aggregate crushing value (ACV) of at least 15-25% and an aggregate impact value (AIV) of 12-25%, thereby improving its mechanical properties compared to untreated RCA. In one embodiment herein, the method for enhancing the properties of RCA is adaptable for industrial-scale implementation, thereby ensuring cost-effectiveness, minimal environmental impact, and enhanced sustainability in construction applications.

[0035] Various embodiments of the present invention will be described in reference to the accompanying drawings. Wherever possible, same or similar reference numerals are used in the drawings and the description to refer to the same or like parts or steps.

[0036] The present disclosure has been made with a view towards solving the problem with the prior art described above, and it is an object of the present invention to provide a method for enhancing the properties of recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) by integrating chemical and physical treatments to improve its strength, density, durability, and compatibility with cementitious matrices.

[0037] According to an exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 1A refers to a screenshot 102 depicting the process of obtaining the RCA from construction and demolition waste. The method improves the mechanical properties of the RCA, such as aggregate crushing value (ACV), aggregate impact value (AIV), and bulk density, making it comparable to natural aggregates. The method enhances the interfacial transition zone (ITZ) between the RCA and cement paste, thereby ensuring better bonding and higher structural integrity in concrete applications. The method is scalable and cost-effective, which allows for industrial-scale RCA processing without excessive energy consumption or high operational costs.

[0038] In one embodiment herein, the process of obtaining recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) from construction and demolition (C&D) waste involves a series of mechanical operations aimed at efficiently recovering and processing concrete debris for reuse in sustainable construction applications. The method comprises multiple sequential stages, such as collection, primary crushing, sieving, and stockpiling, each of which plays a crucial role in ensuring the production of high-quality RCA suitable for further treatment or direct utilization.

[0039] The process begins with the collection of waste concrete debris from construction and demolition sites. The sourced waste primarily consists of hardened concrete elements such as slabs, beams, columns, and structural foundations. These concrete pieces often contain residual mortar, steel reinforcements, and contaminants like dust, plaster, and other construction materials. To ensure an efficient recycling process, the collected debris undergoes a preliminary manual or mechanical sorting operation, where unwanted materials such as wood, plastic, and metals are removed. This step is essential for minimizing impurities in the final RCA product and improving its overall quality.

[0040] Following the initial sorting, the large concrete chunks are subjected to primary crushing using a jaw crusher, as depicted in the screenshot 102. The jaw crusher consists of two metal plates, one stationary and the other movable, which apply compressive force to fracture the concrete into smaller, more manageable fragments. An operator manually feeds the collected concrete debris into the crusher’s intake hopper, thereby ensuring a continuous flow of material. As the machine operates, the rotating mechanical jaws exert high-pressure crushing forces on the concrete pieces, progressively breaking them down into coarse aggregates. During this stage, the residual mortar and cementitious paste adhering to the natural aggregates are partially dislodged, although a significant portion remains attached. The crushed material, comprising a mix of coarse and fine aggregates, is then discharged beneath the crusher, forming a pile of fragmented RCA ready for further refinement.

[0041] According to another exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 1B refers to a screenshot 104 depicting the RCA without any treatment. Once the concrete has undergone primary crushing, the resulting material is transferred to a sieving and grading station, as illustrated in the screenshot 104. This step is critical in refining the RCA by separating aggregates into different size fractions using a wire mesh screen with varying aperture sizes. The sieving unit, constructed using a sturdy wooden frame and multiple layers of mesh, allows aggregates of specific dimensions to pass through while retaining larger particles on the upper surface.

[0042] The RCA is categorized based on particle size, with coarser aggregates remaining at the top and finer fractions accumulating below. This classification enhances the uniformity of RCA and facilitates its use in various construction applications, such as road sub-base layers, non-structural concrete mixes, or as a partial replacement for natural aggregates. Fine particles, such as dust and micro-fragments, are eliminated to prevent excessive water absorption and porosity in concrete applications. The removal of these fines helps in enhancing the durability and mechanical properties of the final concrete product.

[0043] After sieving, the sorted RCA is collected and stockpiled for further processing or direct use in low-strength construction applications. At this stage, the aggregates still retain a significant amount of adhered mortar, which negatively impacts their mechanical properties, such as strength, density, porosity, and water absorption capacity. Although untreated RCA can be used in non-structural applications like road base layers and backfilling material, its performance remains inferior to natural aggregates due to the presence of micro-cracks and high porosity.

[0044] To address these limitations, further enhancement treatments, such as chemical immersion, mechanical milling, ultrasonic cavitation, or thermal processing, may be applied to improve RCA's properties before its incorporation into high-performance concrete mixtures. The untreated RCA obtained from this method serves as a base material for subsequent physical and chemical modification techniques, thereby ensuring sustainable resource utilization in the construction industry.

[0045] According to another exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 2A refers to a screenshot 202 depicting the RCA after physical treatments. In one embodiment herein, the figure showcases recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) that has undergone physical treatment processes to enhance its quality and usability in construction applications. The physical treatments typically include mechanical methods such as crushing, sieving, and washing to remove impurities such as dust, adhered mortar, and unwanted debris. The aggregates in the image appear relatively uniform in size, indicating a well-controlled sieving process. The removal of loose particles and weak mortar layers improves the strength and durability of the RCA, making it more suitable for reuse in concrete production. The physical treatment enhances the gradation and overall performance of the recycled aggregates, ensuring better bonding characteristics in concrete mixes.

[0046] According to another exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 2B refers to a screenshot 204 depicting the RCA after chemical treatments. In another embodiment herein, the figure illustrates RCA that has undergone chemical treatment to further improve its properties. Chemical treatments involve the application of solutions such as acid washing, carbonation, or alkali-based treatments to dissolve and weaken the old adhered mortar. The visible difference in the appearance of the aggregates suggests the removal of some cementitious paste, reducing the porosity of the material and enhancing its mechanical strength. Chemical treatment significantly improves the density, reduces water absorption, and enhances the overall performance of RCA in structural applications. The treatment ensures that the RCA can be used in higher-grade concrete mixes with improved durability and strength.

[0047] According to an exemplary embodiment of the invention, FIG. 3 refers to a flowchart 300 of a method for enhancing the properties of the RCA. At step 302, the RCA is immersed in a citric acid solution at a concentration of at least 1% to 10% to dissolve residual mortar, thereby obtaining an acid-treated RCA. In one embodiment herein, the citric acid immersion is conducted at a temperature between 25°C and 60°C to reaction kinetics while preserving the RCA structural integrity.

[0048] In one embodiment of the present invention, citric acid is employed as a targeted chemical treatment to selectively dissolve the residual mortar that remains adhered to RCA surfaces. The presence of residual mortar contributes to RCA’s high porosity and reduced mechanical strength by introducing weak zones within the aggregate. The citric acid solution chemically reacts with calcium-based compounds in the mortar, effectively breaking down these components and facilitating their removal. This treatment significantly reduces the porosity of RCA, resulting in improved mechanical performance. The use of citric acid in this invention provides an eco-friendly alternative to stronger acids such as hydrochloric acid (HCl), making the process more sustainable while achieving similar efficiency in mortar reduction. The removal of residual mortar exposes the natural aggregate core, which is denser and mechanically superior, thereby enhancing the overall strength and durability of RCA-based concrete.

[0049] In one embodiment herein, the RCA is subjected to an advanced vibratory milling process, which employs controlled vibrations to refine the particle shape and eliminate micro-cracks. This mechanical treatment enhances the aggregate’s surface texture, allowing for superior adhesion to the cement paste in new concrete mixtures. The controlled abrasive forces generated during vibratory milling ensure the removal of weak residual impurities, resulting in RCA with a uniform particle size distribution. This uniformity significantly enhances the workability and mechanical performance of RCA-based concrete. Experimental studies conducted in accordance with this invention have demonstrated that vibratory milling can increase the compressive strength of RCA-based concrete by up to 10% while reducing surface roughness, ensuring improved structural performance.

[0050] At step 304, the acid-treated RCA is subjected to vibratory milling at a frequency range of at least 10 Hz to 50 Hz and an impact force of at least 50 N to 500 N for a time period of 10 to 120 min to refine particle morphology, eliminate micro-cracks, and enhance surface texture, thereby obtaining a milled RCA. In one embodiment herein, the vibratory milling intensity is adjusted based on the level of contamination and aggregate size distribution to maximize surface refinement.

[0051] At step 306, the milled RCA is treated with a sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution at a concentration of at least 1% to 8%, optionally combined with ultrasonic cavitation, to detach residual mortar and enhance surface densification, thereby obtaining NaOH-treated RCA. In one embodiment herein, the ultrasonic cavitation is applied during the NaOH treatment at a frequency of at least 20 kHz to 40 kHz to enhance mortar detachment efficiency, thereby leading to improved bonding characteristics in cementitious applications.

[0052] In another embodiment herein, the sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is utilized to further enhance RCA properties by performing a dual-function treatment. Firstly, NaOH neutralizes any acidic residues remaining from the citric acid treatment phase, thereby ensuring that the RCA maintains a stable pH balance. Secondly, the NaOH actively dissolves and removes organic impurities and weak hydrated cement phases present in the adhered mortar. The chemical interaction between NaOH and the siliceous and alumina-rich compounds in the mortar enhances the reactivity of the RCA surface, thereby leading to better bonding with the cementitious matrix in new concrete applications. In one embodiment herein, alkali-treated RCA exhibits up to 30% lower water absorption compared to untreated aggregates. This improvement is attributed to the sealing effect created by alkali reactions, which densify the RCA surface, thereby improving the durability and long-term performance of RCA-based concrete.

[0053] At step 308, the NaOH-treated RCA is rinsed to remove chemical residues, thereby performing post-treatment drying at a controlled temperature. In one embodiment herein, the NaOH treatment is conducted for a time period of at least 30 min to 4 hr depending on the contamination level and surface composition of the RCA. In one embodiment herein, the post-treatment drying is conducted at an ambient temperature of at least 120°C to achieve optimal moisture reduction while preserving the RCA structural integrity.

[0054] Further, at step 310, the NaOH-treated RCA is heated by applying controlled thermal cycling at a temperature of at least 100°C to 200°C for a time period of at least 30 min to 3 hr, followed by cooling, to reduce porosity and improve aggregate toughness, thereby obtaining an enhanced RCA with reduced water absorption, increased density, and improved compatibility with cementitious matrices. In one embodiment herein, the thermal cycling process involves gradual cooling using air, water, or liquid nitrogen to prevent thermal shock and microstructural damage. In one embodiment herein, the enhanced RCA exhibits a water absorption reduction from 5-10% to 1.5-4.5% and an increase in bulk density from 1200-1500 kg/m³ to 1500-1800 kg/m³.

[0055] In yet another embodiment herein, the RCA is subjected to a precisely controlled thermal cycling process to enhance its internal structure. This method involves subjecting RCA to alternating heating and cooling cycles under controlled conditions. During the heating phase, moisture and weak hydrated cement phases within the aggregate structure are effectively removed. The subsequent rapid cooling induces thermal shock, which modifies the microstructure of the RCA, thereby eliminating internal microcracks and increasing aggregate density. This thermal cycling treatment significantly reduces the porosity of the RCA while improving its mechanical toughness. The thermal cycling treatment has demonstrated that thermal cycling can decrease RCA porosity by 15–25% and enhance its resistance to freeze-thaw cycles. These improvements make RCA more suitable for use in structural concrete applications exposed to harsh environmental conditions, ensuring long-term durability and reliability.

[0056] In one embodiment herein, the treated RCA achieves an aggregate crushing value (ACV) of at least 15-25% and an aggregate impact value (AIV) of 12-25%, thereby improving its mechanical properties compared to untreated RCA. In one embodiment herein, the method for enhancing the properties of RCA is adaptable for industrial-scale implementation, thereby ensuring cost-effectiveness, minimal environmental impact, and enhanced sustainability in construction applications. ABSTRACT: Title: Method for preparing Nutrient-Rich Functional Food Products from Wild Yam Tubers The present disclosure proposes a method for preparing nutrient-rich functional food products from wild yam tubers, which include Dioscorea pubera and Dioscorea pentaphylla, for use in bakery applications such as cookies and namkeen. The method enhances the commercial viability of underutilized wild yam tubers by transforming them into marketable functional food products. The method enables cost-effective production of bakery products using nutrient-dense wild yam tubers, reducing reliance on conventional ingredients. The method promotes value addition to wild yam tubers, creating new revenue streams for farmers, small-scale industries, and food processing enterprises. The method encourages the sustainable utilization of wild yam resources, supporting tribal communities and rural economies through commercial food production. The method enhances food security by promoting the consumption of neglected and underutilized crops, contributing to dietary diversity and improved nutrition.

Field of the invention:
[0001] The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of food technology and functional food processing, in specific, relates to a method for preparing nutrient-rich functional food products from wild yam tubers, which include Dioscorea pubera and Dioscorea pentaphylla, for use in bakery applications such as cookies and namkeen.
Background of the invention:
[0002] Millions of people worldwide face food insecurity and malnutrition due to inadequate access to staple foods. This lack of nutritional diversity results in widespread dietary deficiencies, impacting overall health and well-being. In response, there is a growing emphasis on exploring alternative food sources and agricultural diversification as sustainable solutions to address these challenges. Among the many underutilized crops, wild yam (Dioscorea spp.) has long been an essential food source for tribal and forest-dwelling communities, particularly during periods of food scarcity. The ability of wild yams to grow in diverse and often harsh environmental conditions makes them a resilient and valuable resource in ensuring food security and nutritional sufficiency.
[0003] Wild yam species, belonging to the Dioscoreaceae family, encompass over 600 varieties globally, many of which are still largely unexplored for commercial applications. Traditionally, wild yams have been consumed by indigenous communities for their nutritional benefits, medicinal properties, and livelihood support. They are recognized for their high starch content, proteins, lipids, vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and dietary fiber. Additionally, certain bioactive compounds, such as diosgenin, present in wild yams have been linked to cognitive enhancement, anti-inflammatory effects, and metabolic health improvements. Despite these benefits, the presence of anti-nutritional factors restricts their widespread consumption, necessitating traditional detoxification methods such as boiling, soaking, roasting, and sun drying to make them safe for human consumption.
[0004] Tribal regions, which are recognized for their rich biodiversity, are home to several wild yam species commonly utilized by local populations. However, limited scientific documentation exists regarding their traditional processing techniques, consumption patterns, and potential for value addition. While wild yams have been studied in regions like Nepal, Nigeria, and China, their commercial potential remains largely untapped in many indigenous communities. Addressing this gap through scientific research, value addition, and market integration can enhance their acceptance as functional foods in mainstream diets.
[0005] Functional foods are defined as dietary products that provide health benefits beyond basic nutrition by incorporating bioactive components. The demand for such foods is rapidly increasing due to their potential to prevent lifestyle diseases, improve gut health, and enhance overall well-being. The food industry is actively seeking nutrient-rich, affordable, and consumer-friendly products, particularly in the ready-to-eat segment. Bakery items such as cookies are widely accepted across all age groups due to their convenience, taste, and longer shelf life. Previous research has successfully incorporated functional ingredients into cookies, namkeen, and other snack products using sweet potatoes, cassava, taro, and elephant-foot yams, demonstrating the feasibility of value-added tuber-based products.
[0006] Despite the economic and cultural significance of wild yams, their commercial utilization remains minimal due to lack of awareness, processing challenges, and absence of standardized food formulations. Addressing these limitations through scientific interventions, product innovation, and commercialization efforts can unlock the hidden potential of wild yams as a sustainable and health-promoting food source. Developing value-added functional foods from wild yams can enhance nutritional intake, promote gut health, and offer antioxidant benefits, thereby making them suitable for both traditional and modern dietary needs.
[0007] Additionally, the economic impact of promoting wild yam-based functional foods extends beyond nutrition. Many tribal communities depend on forest resources for their livelihood. Integrating wild yams into commercial food production can create economic opportunities for indigenous farmers, fostering sustainable harvesting, agro-processing industries, and rural entrepreneurship. Such initiatives align with global efforts to promote biodiversity conservation, food security, and rural economic development.
[0008] By addressing all the above-mentioned problems, there is a need for a method for preparing nutrient-rich functional food products from wild yam tubers, which include Dioscorea pubera and Dioscorea pentaphylla, for use in bakery applications such as cookies and namkeen. There is a need for a method that enhances the commercial viability of underutilized wild yam tubers by transforming them into marketable functional food products. There is a need for a method that enables cost-effective production of bakery products using nutrient-dense wild yam tubers, reducing reliance on conventional ingredients.
[0009] Additionally, there is also a need for a method that promotes value addition to wild yam tubers, creating new revenue streams for farmers, small-scale industries, and food processing enterprises. There is a need for a method that encourages the sustainable utilization of wild yam resources, supporting tribal communities and rural economies through commercial food production. There is a need for a method that introduces health-focused, functional bakery products to the market, catering to the growing demand for nutritional snacks and plant-based alternatives. Further, there is also a need for a method that enhances food security by promoting the consumption of neglected and underutilized crops, contributing to dietary diversity and improved nutrition.

ABSTRACT: Title: A Litchi Quality Assessment and Sorting System Using a Fusion of Olfaction and Machine Vision The present disclosure proposes a system (100) that utilizes aroma analysis and digital image processing techniques for grading and sorting litchi fruits. The system (100) for grading and sorting litchi fruits comprises a hopper (102), a conveyor unit (104), an odor sensing unit (112), a vision inspection unit (114), a processing unit (116), plurality of actuators (120) and a control unit (126). The proposed grading and sorting system (100) for litchi fruits that can be operated by any unskilled person. The proposed system (100) delivers quality analysis results as per different export quality standards and generates a report. The proposed system (100) is non-invasive, and reliable. Field of the invention:
[0001] The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of automated quality assessment and sorting of agricultural commodities, and in specific, relates to a system that utilizes aroma analysis and digital image processing techniques for grading and sorting litchi fruits.
Background of the invention:
[0002] Lychee (Litchi chinensis), also spelled as litchi or lichi, is a delicious and juicy fruit of excellent quality. Botanically, it belongs to the Sapindaceae family. Lychee is native to Southeast Asia, is grown commercially in China and India, and has been a favorite fruit of the Cantonese since ancient times. The spread of litchi to other parts of the world was rather slow, probably due to its soil and climatic requirements and the short lifespan of its seed. Litchi reached India through Myanmar and the Northeast region during the 18th century.
[0003] India is the second-largest producer of litchi in the world after China. Other major producing countries include Thailand, Australia, South Africa, Madagascar, and Florida in the United States. Among fruit crops, litchi ranks seventh in area and ninth in production but is sixth in terms of value in India. The food value of litchi primarily lies in its sugar content, which varies by variety. The fruit is also rich in vitamin B1, riboflavin, and vitamin C, apart from proteins (0.7%), fats (0.3%), carbohydrates (9.4%), minerals (0.7%), fibrous matter (2.25%), calcium (0.21%), phosphorus (0.31%), iron (0.03%), and carotene.
[0004] Litchi makes an excellent canned fruit, and a highly flavored squash is prepared from litchi fruits, which is used during summers. Various other products such as pickles, preserves, and wine are also made from litchi in China. Dried litchi, commonly called litchi-nut, is very popular among the Chinese. The fruits are oval to round, strawberry-red in color, and about 25 mm (approximately 1 inch) in diameter. The brittle outer covering encloses a translucent white fleshy aril and one large seed. Although India is the second-largest producer of litchi fruit, its share in the global export market is very low due to its short shelf life. There is a need to pack only sorted, sound fruit to ensure a longer shelf life under various packaging conditions.
[0005] In existing technology, an apparatus is an automated fruit sorting system integrates image and odor analysis for quality assessment. It features a camera, an image analysis unit, a sorting mechanism, and an odor-detection chamber. However, the automated fruit sorting system processes one fruit at a time, making it time-consuming. Moreover, the automated fruit sorting system captures and analyzes all fruits, thereby increasing overall operational complexity.
[0006] Therefore, there is a need for a grading and sorting system that can be operated by any unskilled person. There is also a need for a grading and sorting system that is non-invasive, and reliable. There is also a need for a grading and sorting system that consumes less time. There is also a need for a grading and sorting system that isolates litchi fruits, thereby minimizing the risk of overlapping. Further, there is also a need for a grading and sorting system that can achieve quick and accurate micro-damage detection.
Objectives of the invention:
[0007] The primary objective of the invention is to provide a system that utilizes aroma analysis and digital image processing techniques for grading and sorting litchi fruits.
[0008] Another objective of the invention is to provide a system that integrates a fusion of an odor sensing unit and a vision inspection unit to achieve quick and accurate micro-damage detection.
[0009] The other objective of the invention is to provide a system comprises a conveyor unit that isolates litchi fruits while moving on a conveyor belt, thereby minimizing the risk of overlapping.
[0010] The other objective of the invention is to provide a system that comprises the odor sensing unit to enhance aroma release from the litchi fruit during analysis.
[0011] The other objective of the invention is to provide a grading and sorting system for litchi fruits that can be operated by any unskilled person.
[0012] Yet another objective of the invention is to provide a system that delivers quality analysis results as per different export quality standards and generates a report.
[0013] Further objective of the invention is to provide a system that is non-invasive and reliable.
Summary of the invention:
[0014] The present disclosure proposes a litchi quality assessment and sorting system using a fusion of olfaction and machine vision. The following presents a simplified summary in order to provide a basic understanding of some aspects of the claimed subject matter. This summary is not an extensive overview. It is not intended to identify key/critical elements or to delineate the scope of the claimed subject matter. Its sole purpose is to present some concepts in a simplified form as a prelude to the more detailed description that is presented later.
[0015] In order to overcome the above deficiencies of the prior art, the present disclosure is to solve the technical problem to provide a system that utilizes aroma analysis and digital image processing techniques for grading and sorting litchi fruits.
[0016] According to an aspect, the invention provides a litchi quality assessment and sorting system using a fusion of olfaction and machine vision. In one embodiment herein, the system for grading and sorting litchi fruits comprises a hopper, a conveyor unit, an odor sensing unit, a vision inspection unit, a processing unit, plurality of actuators and a control unit.
[0017] In one embodiment herein, the hopper is configured to enable a user to place plurality of litchi fruits. In one embodiment herein, the conveyor unit is configured to receive the plurality of litchi fruits from the hopper. The conveyor unit comprises a conveyor belt. In one embodiment herein, the conveyor belt is rotatably positioned between a pair of conveyor pulleys. The conveyor belt is configured to be rotated upon activation of a driving unit for transferring the plurality of litchi fruits. The conveyor belt having spaced grooves for discretely positioning the plurality of litchi fruits.
[0018] In one embodiment herein, the proximity sensor is positioned on the conveyor unit 104. The proximity sensor is configured to transmit a signal to the control unit upon detecting a metal member on the conveyor belt for halting the conveyor belt at predefined positions. In one embodiment herein, the odor sensing unit positioned on the conveyor belt. The odor sensing unit is configured to detect and analyze aroma volatiles from each of the litchi fruit, thereby separating the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles from non-aromatic litchi fruits based on predefined quality standards. The odor sensing unit comprises at least two sensor tubes and a suction fan.
[0019] In one embodiment herein, the at least two sensor tubes are configured to detect the aroma volatiles from each of the litchi fruit such as benzyl alcohol, linalool, and geraniol, and convert the detected data into a digital signal for categorization. In one embodiment herein, the suction fan is configured to purge residual aroma molecules upon detecting the aroma volatiles of the plurality of litchi fruits to prevent cross-contamination. In one embodiment herein, the vision inspection unit is configured to capture the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles and analyze captured data for detecting quality parameters of each of the litchi fruit, thereby enabling to categorize the plurality of litchi fruits.
[0020] The vision inspection unit is equipped with plurality of illuminating units for providing a controlled lighting environment to detect defects on the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles such as cracks, discoloration, fungal infections and borer damage using an image processing algorithm. The vision inspection unit comprises a capturing unit for capturing and analysing the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles to extract quality parameters such as perimeter, diameter, area, and color uniformity for grading using an image segmentation algorithm.
[0021] In one embodiment herein, the processing unit is configured to perform categorization of the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles into one or more categories based on agricultural quality standards and marketing rules. In one embodiment herein, the plurality of actuators is configured to be activated for picking the plurality of litchi fruits from the conveyor belt to place into one or more containers through dispensing channels upon completion of categorization by the vision inspection unit.
[0022] In one embodiment herein, the control unit is configured to automatically control grading and sorting operations performed by the system through the odor sensing unit, the vision inspection unit and the processing unit, and operate the conveyor unit at regular interval of times for taking the aroma volatiles from the plurality of litchi fruits for analyzing by the odor sensing unit. The control unit is configured to activate the driving unit for rotating the conveyor belt to transfer the plurality of litchi fruits from one place to other place. The control unit is configured to receive the signal from the proximity sensor upon detecting the metal member to halt the conveyor belt. The control unit is configured to activate the actuators for picking the plurality of litchi fruits from the conveyor belt and transfer them into the one or more containers through the dispensing channels using the air blowing mechanism upon completion of categorization by the vision inspection unit.
[0023] In one embodiment herein, the hopper is equipped with a roller and a brush member to ensure uniform dispensing of the plurality of litchi fruits onto the conveyor belt in a non-overlapping manner. In one embodiment herein, the rejected litchi fruits are automatically removed from the conveyor belt using an air blow ejection mechanism operated by the plurality of actuators. In one embodiment herein, the system for grading and sorting litchi fruits comprises a graphical user interface (GUI) for monitoring real-time analysis results, storing data, and generating quality reports for each batch of litchi fruits.
[0024] According to another aspect, the invention provides a method for operating the system for grading and sorting litchi fruits. At one step, the hopper receives the plurality of litchi fruits and dispenses them onto the conveyor belt. At one step, the control unit activates the driving unit to rotate the pair of conveyor pulleys, thereby moving the plurality of litchi fruits from one end to other end. At one step, the control unit receives the signal from the proximity sensor upon detecting the metal member on the conveyor belt and operates the driving unit to halt the conveyor belt.
[0025] At one step, the odor sensing unit detects and analyses the aroma volatiles from the plurality of litchi fruits using the at least two sensor tubes, thereby separating the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles from non-aromatic litchi fruits based on predefined quality standards. At one step, the control unit activates the plurality of actuators to remove the non-aromatic litchi fruits from the conveyor belt, thereby operating the driving unit to move the conveyor belt upon performing the aroma detection. At one step, the control unit receives the signal from the proximity sensor upon detecting the metal member and operates the driving unit to halt the conveyor belt.
[0026] At one step, the vision inspection unit captures the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles and analysing the captured data to assess color, size and shape. At one step, the processing unit categorizes the plurality of litchi fruits that exhibit desirable aroma volatiles into one or more categories based on agricultural quality standards and marketing rules. At one step, the control unit activates the plurality of actuators to direct the processed fruits into the one or more containers of dispensing channels by the air blowing mechanism upon completion of categorization by the vision inspection unit.

The at least six MOS gas sensors comprises a sampling unit, a detection unit and a controller. These variations are converted into measurable signals, enabling the system 100 to differentiate between various aroma compositions.

[0093] In one example embodiment herein, the odor sensing unit 112 is responsible for monitoring the smell and aroma emitted from the plurality of litchi fruits. Before initiating the analysis of the odor sensing unit 112, the at least two sensor tubes 156 undergo a pre-heating process, which lasts for at least one hour. This step, known as the pre-heat phase, ensures the stability and accuracy of the at least two sensor tubes 156. Once pre-heating is completed, the conveyor belt 106 is activated, and the plurality of litchi fruits is poured into the hopper 102. For accurate analysis, the plurality of litchi fruits is prepared by detaching them from the stem through a clockwise twisting motion at the notch point.
[0094] As the plurality of litchi fruits reaches the designated position under the odor sensing unit 112, the at least two sensor tubes 156 are exposed to the volatile odor vapors. The odor sensing unit 112 ensures a constant exposure rate across the at least two sensor tubes 156. The response signals generated by the at least two sensor tubes 156 are conditioned and processed through an appropriate electronic circuit. These signals are then transmitted to an intelligent pattern recognition engine i.e., the olfactory processing unit 142 for classification, analysis, and declaration of results.
[0095] In one embodiment herein, the vision inspection unit 114 is designed to replicate the visual perception of an experienced litchi taster or expert. A customized image capturing setup is integrated into the vision inspection unit 114, where the vision inspection unit 114 facilitates image acquisition, analysis, and grading of the plurality of litchi fruits based on predefined criteria. The application autonomously captures images of the plurality of litchi fruits as they move along the conveyor belt 106. The output of the image analysis module provides an assessment of different quality attributes, along with the corresponding grade of the each litchi fruit.
[0096] The image analysis process involves several sequential steps. At first, image acquisition, utilizes the capturing unit 140 i.e., a digital camera is mounted inside the vision inspection unit 114. The conveyor belt 106 is segmented into multiple subsections using white-colored spaced grooves 164, thereby ensuring a clear distinction between the plurality of litchi fruits. When the litchi fruit halts under the vision inspection unit 114, the capturing unit 140 captures images of the conveyor belt 106 and transmits them to the image analysis module. The second step, image cropping, eliminates unnecessary background areas.
[0097] Only the region enclosed by the white strip (clit) is extracted for processing. Next, the image undergoes plane extraction, where the grayscale plane is isolated to enhance meaningful feature extraction. The grayscale image is derived using the equation: New grayscale image = (0.3 * R) + (0.59 * G) + (0.11 * B), wherein the green channel has the highest contribution.
[0098] Following grayscale conversion, the image is processed for noise reduction using a median filter, which primarily eliminates salt-and-pepper noise. A 3×3 pixel region is analyzed for noise removal. In the image segmentation step, a simple thresholding technique converts the image into a binary format. The background is assigned a pixel value of 0, while the litchi area is represented with a pixel value of 255. Any discoloration within the sample appears as a 0-pixel region. Morphology analysis is then conducted, involving various filtering techniques to refine the image.
[0099] Initially, small unwanted objects are removed by setting a minimum area threshold. Subsequently, any gaps in the object’s border are filled, followed by erosion to eliminate residual noise and artifacts. The refined image is then processed further. Contour detection is performed on the processed black-and-white image using a Quick Mask technique. The contour of the litchi fruit is identified by applying an edge-detection kernel, represented as:

[0100] Once contours are detected, object identification is carried out by analyzing the size information of each contoured region. The length and breadth of each object are measured, and any sample with a breadth less than 23 mm is discarded from further analysis. The area of the litchi fruit is then calculated by counting the total number of pixels enclosed within the contour. The vision inspection unit 114 extracts seven key size and shape features, including perimeter, diameter, equivalent rectangle parameters, total area, and hole area. In addition to shape analysis, the color attributes of the litchi fruit are evaluated by counting the number of good and bad pixels.
[0101] A ratio is calculated to determine the acceptability of the litchi fruit. If this ratio exceeds a predefined threshold, the litchi fruit is classified as rejected. A mapping mechanism between real-world data and application data is embedded within the quality analysis software. For litchi classified as "Extra Class," the fruit must exhibit uniform coloration. "Class I" allows slight defects in color, provided they do not exceed an area of 0.25 cm², while "Class II" permits defects up to 0.50 cm². Threshold pixel intensity values are defined to enforce these classification criteria.
[0102] The final stage of image analysis involves object classification. The extracted size parameters are stored in a database, where decision-making algorithms assess and generate the final grading results. ABSTRACT: Title: Integrated Self-Cooking and Diet Management System for Customized Meal Preparation and Method of Operation The present disclosure proposes an integrated self-cooking and diet management system (100) that recommends personalized meal plans and assists in meal preparation with automated cooking capabilities. The integrated self-cooking and diet management system (100) comprises an automatic cooking device (102), and a computing device (116) in communication with the automatic cooking device (102) through a server (112) via a network (114). The integrated self-cooking and diet management system (100) generates AI-driven, customized diet plans based on user-specific health parameters such as BMI, age, allergies, dietary preferences, cultural restrictions, and medical conditions. The integrated self-cooking and diet management system (100) integrates biometric sensors, such as glucose monitors, for tracking real-time health metrics and dynamically adjusting diet recommendations accordingly.

Field of the invention:
[0001] The present disclosure generally relates to the technical field of automated cooking systems and diet planning, and in specific relates to an integrated self-cooking and diet management system that recommends personalized meal plans and assists in meal preparation with automated cooking capabilities.
Background of the invention:
[0002] Nutrition plays a fundamental role in human health and well-being. A well-balanced diet not only helps in preventing chronic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, and cardiovascular disorders but also supports overall physical and cognitive development. However, modern lifestyles, time constraints, and a lack of nutritional awareness often lead individuals to make unhealthy dietary choices. Additionally, individuals with dietary restrictions due to allergies, medical conditions, or cultural preferences struggle to find suitable meal options tailored to their needs.
[0003] Malnutrition, in both undernutrition and overnutrition forms, remains a global challenge. According to health organizations, millions of people suffer from deficiencies in essential nutrients, while others face obesity-related health risks due to poor eating habits. The issue is especially pronounced in low- and middle-income countries, where access to proper nutrition is limited. Additionally, many individuals lack the time, skills, or resources to prepare healthy meals at home, further exacerbating the problem.
[0004] People with specific medical conditions, such as diabetes or food allergies, require personalized diet plans, but existing solutions often rely on manual meal tracking, which can be inconvenient and prone to human error. Moreover, individuals unfamiliar with cooking find it challenging to prepare nutritious meals, leading to dependence on processed foods that contribute to health issues.
[0005] Mobile diet-tracking applications help users monitor calorie intake and suggest dietary improvements based on manually entered data. Smart Kitchen Appliances such as smart blenders, automatic cookers, and programmable pressure cookers assist users in meal preparation with preset cooking modes. AI-driven meal planning services analyze dietary needs and recommend meal plans, often integrating with grocery delivery services. Wearable Health Devices like continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) and fitness trackers monitor vital signs to provide insights into health and nutrition needs.
[0006] Despite advancements in diet tracking, smart cooking, and health monitoring, existing solutions have several limitations. Most current technologies operate in isolation, requiring users to manually combine data from diet tracking apps, health monitors, and cooking appliances. While some smart kitchen appliances assist in cooking, they still require significant user intervention, particularly for ingredient preparation and cooking sequence control. Many diet-planning applications rely on generic databases and fail to provide truly personalized recommendations based on real-time biometric data. Manually inputting food intake, tracking portion sizes, and interpreting nutritional information can be cumbersome for users, reducing long-term adherence. Current AI-driven nutrition solutions provide static recommendations without learning from user preferences, habits, or changing health conditions.
[0007] Therefore, there is a need for an integrated self-cooking and diet management system that recommends personalized meal plans and assists in meal preparation with automated cooking capabilities. There is also a need for an integrated self-cooking and diet management system that should dynamically adjust dietary recommendations based on real-time health data, dietary restrictions, and personal preferences while simplifying the cooking process for users. There is also a need for an integrated self-cooking and diet management system that seamlessly integrates multiple functions, including AI-driven diet planning and biometric health tracking, into a single, user-friendly solution while also functioning as an autonomous cooking assistant. This innovation eliminates the need for multiple separate devices and applications, providing a seamless and efficient approach to healthy eating.
