Description:Field of the Invention
The present invention relates to the field of nutritional biotechnology. More particularly, the present invention relates nano-based artificial diet for silkworm, Bombyx mori L. for improved growth of silkworm round the year and better silk production in terms of silk yield and strength.

Background of the Invention
The background information herein below relates to the present disclosure but is not necessarily prior art.

Sericulture involves cultivating mulberry trees and rearing of silkworms for silk production, providing a regular supply of mulberry leaves and supporting over 30 million people globally, primarily in China, India, Uzbekistan, Brazil, Japan, and Vietnam. China and India alone account for 26 million sericulture farmers. In 2022-23, India produced 36,453 metric tons of raw mulberry silk, valued at over 17 billion Indian rupees, yet domestic production remains insufficient to meet demand. Sericulture faces significant challenges, particularly the seasonal availability and quality variation of mulberry leaves, which are crucial for silkworm health and productivity. Silkworms (Bombyx mori L.) rely exclusively on mulberry leaves, whose nutritional value is affected by weather, soil conditions, pests, diseases, and farming practices, impacting silk yield and quality. Factors such as nutrient levels in different cultivars, optimal harvesting times, and nutrient concentrations in younger and top leaves further influence mulberry leaf nutrition. Pests and diseases also lead to higher production costs due to labor, pesticides, and fertilizers, resulting in income instability for farmers. Environmental concerns include significant land and water resource requirements, leading to deforestation, water scarcity, soil degradation, and pollution. The labor-intensive nature of mulberry cultivation exacerbates these challenges, especially with labor shortages. Research and development constraints, such as slower breeding cycles and limited innovation opportunities, hinder progress in sericulture. Supply chain disruptions from natural disasters and market fluctuations can severely impact mulberry leaf production and industry stability. Artificial diets present a promising solution by providing essential nutrients year-round, ensuring sustainable and reliable nutrition for young silkworms. Studies have shown no negative impacts on economic indicators when silkworm larvae are fed artificial diets until the chawki stage. Nano-based products, including titanium dioxide, silver, zinc oxide, and selenium nanoparticles, are gaining traction for enhancing silkworm growth, nutritional absorption, immunity, and general health. These interventions offer advanced and sustainable solutions to traditional silkworm rearing challenges. While no market options for nano-based artificial diets for silkworms currently exist, these diets show potential for maintaining better silkworm health and ensuring a consistent year-round feed supply, eliminating seasonal dependencies. Our results suggest that nano-based diets could revolutionize sericulture by fostering research, accelerating the development of region-specific silkworm breeds, and ensuring sustainable productivity. Collaboration with industry stakeholders is essential for the successful adoption and integration of nano-based diets, making this innovation a potent, safe, and cost-effective alternative poised to gain market momentum.
Sericulture farmers face significant challenges due to the seasonal availability and quality variation of mulberry leaves, which directly impact silkworm health and productivity. The quality of mulberry leaves is crucial for the development and silk production of silkworms (Bombyx mori L.), which depend exclusively on these leaves (Etebari, 2002). However, the nutritional value of mulberry leaves fluctuates based on weather, soil conditions, pests, diseases, and farming practices, affecting the quantity and quality of cocoons and silk produced (Ito, 1978).
The silkworm Bombyx mori is a monophagous insect, feeding exclusively on mulberry leaves. However, high-quality mulberry leaves are available only during specific favorable seasons due to climate, geographical location, and mulberry cultivars. This limited availability restricts year-round silkworm rearing. Fresh mulberry leaves must meet the nutritional needs and preferences of silkworms, but this system faces challenges such as high costs associated with the establishment of mulberry gardens, leaf transportation, preservation, and labor-intensive processes (Hamamura et al., 1959; 1966; Fukuda et al. (1960)). India led the way in creating a semi-synthetic diet called Nutrid at CSR&TI, Mysore, in 2008. However, despite the evolution of five multivoltine and six bivoltine strains by Trivedy et al. in 2001 and 2003, respectively, the results of this initiative did not meet expectations. Hence, artificial diets for silkworms serve as a valuable solution during periods when mulberry leaves are unavailable due to unfavorable climatic conditions. Additionally, they offer researchers an ideal model insect for scientific studies throughout the year. Mulberry leaf nutrition is influenced by several factors, including nutrient levels in different cultivars, optimal harvesting times, higher nutrient concentrations in younger leaves, and more nutrient-rich top leaves (Hu et al., 2013).  Additionally, mulberry plants are susceptible to pests and diseases, leading to higher production costs due to labor, pesticides, and fertilizers, and resulting in income instability. Environmental concerns include significant land and water resource requirements for mulberry cultivation, contributing to deforestation, water scarcity, soil degradation, and water pollution. The labor-intensive nature of mulberry cultivation and leaf harvesting exacerbates these challenges, especially with labor shortages. Nutritional variability in mulberry leaves also affects silkworm health, leading to inconsistencies in silkworm growth and development. Research and development constraints include slower breeding cycles and limited innovation opportunities without a viable artificial diet. Supply chain disruptions from natural disasters and market fluctuations can severely impact mulberry leaf production and industry stability.
The current technology in silkworm rearing faces significant limitations, impacting efficiency, consistency, and profitability in the sericulture industry. Key issues include the absence of a commercially available Nano-Based Silkworm Artificial Diet, leading to missed opportunities for improved nutrient delivery and absorption. Traditional diets result in inconsistent nutrition, causing variable cocoon quality and yield, and nutritional gaps affecting silkworm health and productivity. Additionally, the lack of probiotic-based diets limits the immune response and disease resistance of silkworms, increasing mortality rates and impacting silk quality. The labor-intensive nature of traditional rearing methods further compounds these problems, posing operational challenges and high labor costs. 

To address these challenges, present invention aims to provide Nano-Based Artificial Diet (NBAD) offers a promising solution. This innovative diet uses bioengineered nanoparticles to enhance nutrient absorption and incorporates probiotics to boost immune responses, ensuring healthier and more productive silkworms. The NBAD reduces labor dependency with its easy-to-use design, requiring less frequent feeding, thus lowering labor costs and improving efficiency. By providing standardized nutrition, it ensures consistent cocoon quality and yield, leading to increased productivity and profitability for sericulture farmers. This transformative approach not only enhances the health and productivity of silkworms but also advances silk production methodologies, ensuring a sustainable and profitable future for the sericulture industry.

To formulate test diets for silkworms, the first step is to measure the required amounts of feed ingredients. The process involves mixing the feed ingredients (dried diet), adding water to form a mixture, steaming the mixture, cooling it in a freezer, and transferring the prepared diet to the rearing rooms as needed. The amount of water added to the dried diet is adjusted by multiplying the weighed diet ingredients by a factor of 2.80. 

EXAMPLE 2
The ingredients are mixed thoroughly with distilled water and then steamed in an autoclave at 100°C for 30 minutes. For the first three instars, the temperature and relative humidity are maintained at 30 (±1)°C and 85 (±5) percent RH. The last two larval instars are then fed separately with natural mulberry leaf diet or artificial diet at temperatures of 25 (±1)°C and 75 (±5) percent RH, respectively. Abstract:

The present invention relates to a semi-autonomous robotic system designed for remote inspection, search and rescue, and surveillance applications. The robotic system incorporates a bioinspired multi-segmented body structure with flexible joint mechanisms, enabling efficient navigation through confined spaces, rugged terrains, and debris-filled environments. The system features servo motor-driven wave-like locomotion controlled by an onboard microcontroller, allowing for precise movement coordination. An RF communication module facilitates real-time remote operation, while an integrated camera system provides high-resolution visual feedback for enhanced situational awareness. The robotic system further integrates a sensor-driven autonomy framework comprising touch sensors, infrared sensors, and vision-based sensors, ensuring adaptive environmental perception and obstacle avoidance. The modular design supports easy reconfiguration and maintenance, allowing integration of additional components for specific operational needs. Designed for search and rescue missions, industrial inspections, and surveillance, the robotic system enhances operational efficiency and safety in complex and hazardous environments.

Description:TECHNICAL FIELD
[0001] The present invention relates to the field of robotics, specifically to a semi-autonomous robotic system with integrated camera and radio frequency (RF) communication capabilities. The system is designed for remote inspection, search, and rescue operations in complex environments such as disaster sites, industrial facilities, and surveillance zones. The robotic system incorporates bioinspired biomechanics, modular adaptability, and advanced sensor technology to enhance mobility in confined spaces and rugged terrains, making it highly effective in disaster response, industrial inspection, and security applications.
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
[0002] Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention.  It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art.
[0003] The field of robotics has significantly evolved over the years, playing a crucial role in various industries, including disaster response, industrial inspection, and security surveillance. One of the primary challenges in these domains is the ability to navigate through complex and unpredictable environments, particularly in disaster-stricken areas or confined industrial spaces. Traditional robotic systems often struggle with maneuverability in such conditions due to their rigid structures and limited adaptability. The need for a more flexible, efficient, and reliable robotic system has led to the development of bioinspired designs that mimic the movement patterns of biological organisms, offering enhanced mobility and operational effectiveness.
[0004] Disaster response and search and rescue operations require swift and accurate assessment of hazardous environments, often characterized by collapsed buildings, rubble, and confined spaces where human access is either dangerous or impossible. The inability to deploy rescue personnel in such situations increases the risk of loss of life and delays in locating and assisting trapped individuals. Conventional robotic systems, while useful, are often hindered by obstacles such as uneven terrain, narrow passageways, and debris-filled environments. The challenge of overcoming these limitations has driven researchers and engineers to explore bioinspired robotics, leveraging the adaptability and flexibility observed in natural organisms to create robotic systems capable of navigating through the most challenging terrains.
[0005] Historically, bioinspired robotic systems have drawn influence from various biological creatures, particularly those that exhibit exceptional locomotion abilities in constrained environments. The study of snake-like, insect-inspired, and modular robotic designs has paved the way for the development of multi-segmented robotic systems with enhanced maneuverability. These designs have been particularly beneficial in applications requiring movement through pipelines, tunnels, and collapsed structures. Early robotic systems primarily relied on simple mechanical structures with limited articulation. However, advancements in actuator technology, sensor integration, and artificial intelligence have led to the creation of highly responsive and autonomous robotic systems.
[0006] One of the key technological developments in this field is the incorporation of real-time data transmission and remote control capabilities, enabling human operators to guide robotic systems through hazardous environments. The integration of radio frequency (RF) communication has significantly improved the reliability and range of remote-controlled robotic systems, allowing real-time navigation and data collection. In search and rescue operations, the ability to transmit live video feeds and environmental data to rescue teams is invaluable, as it enables informed decision-making and precise location tracking of survivors. This has also found applications in industrial inspection, where robotic systems are deployed in confined spaces such as pipelines, machinery interiors, and hazardous chemical environments, reducing the risk to human workers.
[0007] The introduction of multi-sensor integration has further enhanced the capabilities of modern robotic systems. Sensors such as infrared, ultrasonic, and visual cameras allow robots to perceive their surroundings, detect obstacles, and navigate autonomously or semi-autonomously. The use of advanced algorithms enables robots to process sensor data in real-time, making adaptive decisions based on environmental conditions. This is particularly useful in disaster response, where robots must traverse unstable terrains, avoid obstacles, and locate survivors efficiently. The addition of touch-sensitive and proximity sensors has further improved the ability of robotic systems to operate in unpredictable environments, reducing the likelihood of mechanical failures and enhancing overall mission success rates.
[0008] Despite these advancements, existing robotic systems still face several challenges in terms of flexibility, adaptability, and operational efficiency. Many traditional robots lack the ability to dynamically adjust their shape and movement to suit varying environmental conditions. Rigid structures and predefined movement patterns often limit the effectiveness of robots in highly complex and cluttered environments. Furthermore, power consumption remains a critical factor, as extended operations require efficient energy management to prevent system failure during critical missions. These challenges have necessitated the development of a novel robotic system that not only overcomes these limitations but also introduces enhanced bioinspired movement, modular adaptability, and intelligent control mechanisms.
[0009] The present invention addresses these issues by introducing a robotic system designed with a highly flexible, multi-segmented body that mimics biological movement patterns, ensuring smooth traversal through tight spaces and uneven terrains. The integration of an advanced RF-controlled navigation system allows precise remote operation, improving maneuverability in otherwise inaccessible areas. Additionally, a real-time camera system provides enhanced situational awareness, allowing operators to monitor environments effectively. The incorporation of an optimized modular design further improves adaptability, enabling the robotic system to adjust its configuration based on specific operational needs. Finally, a sensor-driven autonomy framework enhances environmental perception, enabling intelligent obstacle detection and semi-autonomous navigation. By integrating these advanced features, the present invention aims to provide a highly effective solution for disaster response, industrial inspection, and surveillance applications, ensuring improved safety and efficiency in critical operations.

This robotic system incorporates bioinspired biomechanics, advanced control mechanisms, and real-time communication capabilities to enhance mobility in confined and hazardous environments. By drawing inspiration from natural movement patterns, the invention significantly improves maneuverability in disaster-stricken areas, industrial sites, and security operations, ensuring a more efficient and reliable approach to remote exploration and assessment.
[0018] One of the core features of this invention is its highly flexible, multi-segmented body, which allows the robotic system to traverse through narrow passages, rugged terrains, and debris-filled environments with ease. Unlike conventional robotic systems with rigid structures, this bioinspired design ensures seamless adaptability to complex surroundings, enhancing its effectiveness in search and rescue missions. The segmented structure is powered by precisely controlled servo motors, enabling coordinated motion and efficient traversal of obstacles. The movement mechanism is optimized for energy efficiency, ensuring prolonged operational capability in critical missions.
[0019] The robotic system is equipped with an advanced RF-controlled navigation system, enabling remote operation with minimal latency. This feature is particularly beneficial in hazardous environments where human intervention is limited or impossible. Operators can guide the robotic system through complex terrains using a wireless interface, ensuring real-time control and adaptability. The RF communication module ensures reliable data transmission over extended distances, making it an ideal solution for disaster response teams, industrial inspectors, and security personnel. The ability to navigate remotely in real time significantly enhances the efficiency of search and rescue operations, industrial maintenance, and surveillance activities.
[0020] To further enhance situational awareness, the invention incorporates an integrated camera system capable of capturing and transmitting real-time visual data. The high-resolution camera module provides operators with a clear view of the robot’s surroundings, enabling accurate decision-making in mission-critical scenarios. Whether used for locating survivors in disaster zones, inspecting industrial machinery, or monitoring security-sensitive areas, the real-time video feed ensures comprehensive environmental assessment. The camera module is strategically positioned to provide a wide field of view, reducing blind spots and ensuring optimal coverage of the operational area.
[0021] Another key aspect of the invention is its modular design, which allows for easy assembly, maintenance, and reconfiguration. The modular approach enhances adaptability, enabling the robotic system to be customized based on specific operational requirements. Whether deployed in confined industrial spaces, open disaster zones, or surveillance operations, the system can be adjusted to optimize performance. The modular design also facilitates the integration of additional sensors and accessories, making the invention a versatile solution for diverse applications.
[0022] To ensure autonomous functionality, the robotic system is equipped with a sensor-driven autonomy framework, integrating touch, infrared, and vision-based sensors for enhanced environmental perception. These sensors enable obstacle detection, terrain analysis, and adaptive navigation, allowing the robot to operate with minimal human intervention. The use of advanced algorithms ensures intelligent decision-making, enabling the robotic system to identify and respond to environmental challenges in real time. This feature is particularly useful in scenarios where human guidance is limited, ensuring uninterrupted operation in critical missions.
[0023] Overall, the present invention provides a comprehensive solution for remote inspection, search and rescue operations, and industrial surveillance by integrating bioinspired biomechanics, RF communication, real-time visual monitoring, modular adaptability, and sensor-driven autonomy. By addressing the limitations of traditional robotic systems, this invention enhances mobility, reliability, and efficiency in complex environments, ensuring a highly effective and versatile robotic solution for disaster response, industrial applications, and security operations.

[0031] The present invention relates to a semi-autonomous robotic system designed for remote inspection, search and rescue operations, and surveillance applications. The robotic system is engineered to navigate through confined spaces, rugged terrains, and debris-filled environments by incorporating a bioinspired design, advanced control mechanisms, and real-time sensor-based adaptability. This invention introduces an innovative approach to robotic mobility, ensuring enhanced flexibility, real-time communication, and intelligent perception for mission-critical tasks.
[0032] The robotic system comprises a multi-segmented body structure inspired by the locomotion patterns of biological organisms such as snakes and insects. Each segment is interconnected through a flexible joint mechanism, allowing smooth articulation and controlled movement. The primary structural components of the robotic system are made of high-strength yet lightweight materials such as aluminum and high-grade plastic, ensuring durability while maintaining maneuverability. The flexible body structure enables the robot to adjust its shape dynamically, allowing it to pass through narrow passageways, traverse over obstacles, and operate efficiently in constrained environments. The design is optimized for energy efficiency, ensuring prolonged operational capability in emergency scenarios.
[0033] The movement of the robotic system is controlled by a series of servo motors integrated into each segment, enabling precise articulation and synchronization. The locomotion is based on a wave-like motion pattern, where each segment sequentially follows the preceding segment to achieve smooth and continuous movement. The robot is capable of executing forward, backward, and rotational movements, allowing it to maneuver around obstacles and navigate complex terrains effectively. The motion mechanism is regulated by an onboard microcontroller, which processes movement commands and coordinates motor actuation to achieve efficient navigation. This system ensures stability and minimizes energy consumption while maintaining high maneuverability.
[0034] To enable real-time remote operation, the robotic system is equipped with an advanced RF communication module. This module consists of a transmitter and receiver pair, facilitating seamless data transmission between the robot and a remote operator. The RF-based control system provides a reliable and low-latency communication channel, ensuring that the operator can precisely control the robotic system from a distance. The RF communication module also supports bidirectional data transfer, allowing sensor data, video feeds, and system diagnostics to be transmitted back to the operator in real time. This capability is particularly beneficial in search and rescue missions where immediate feedback is essential for decision-making.
[0035] An integrated camera system enhances the situational awareness of the operator by providing real-time visual feedback. The camera module, positioned strategically on the robotic system, captures high-resolution images and video streams, transmitting them to a remote monitoring station. This allows operators to assess the environment, identify obstacles, and locate individuals in need of rescue. The camera module is capable of adjusting its focus and orientation, ensuring optimal visibility in low-light conditions and cluttered environments. The real-time visual feedback provided by the camera system significantly improves the effectiveness of search and rescue operations, industrial inspections, and surveillance tasks.
[0036] The robotic system incorporates a modular design that allows for easy assembly, maintenance, and reconfiguration. Each segment of the robot can be detached and replaced as needed, ensuring flexibility in adapting the system for different operational scenarios. The modular approach enables the integration of additional sensors, actuators, or payloads depending on the specific application requirements. This adaptability enhances the versatility of the robotic system, making it suitable for a wide range of environments, including disaster sites, industrial facilities, and security-sensitive areas.
[0037] A key feature of the robotic system is its sensor-driven autonomy framework, which enables intelligent environmental perception and adaptive navigation. The system is equipped with multiple sensors, including touch sensors, infrared sensors, and vision-based sensors, which collectively enhance its ability to detect obstacles, assess terrain conditions, and make real-time navigation decisions. The touch sensors allow the robot to identify physical barriers and adjust its movement accordingly, preventing collisions and ensuring smooth traversal. The infrared sensors provide depth perception, enabling the robot to detect variations in surface elevation and adjust its locomotion strategy accordingly. The vision-based sensors, in combination with the onboard camera, enable the robot to recognize objects and navigate through complex environments with greater precision.
[0038] The control and processing unit of the robotic system is powered by an Arduino microcontroller, which serves as the central processing hub for movement coordination, sensor data processing, and communication management. The microcontroller is programmed with advanced algorithms that govern movement patterns, sensor data fusion, and decision-making processes. The embedded software includes motion planning algorithms that optimize the robot’s trajectory based on real-time environmental inputs. This ensures efficient navigation and obstacle avoidance while minimizing energy consumption. The control system supports both manual and semi-autonomous operation modes, allowing the robotic system to function effectively in different scenarios.
[0039] The robotic system's energy efficiency is enhanced through a combination of optimized motor control, power-efficient sensor integration, and lightweight material selection. The servo motors are designed to consume minimal power while delivering precise movement control, ensuring prolonged operational endurance. The modular battery system provides a reliable power source, supporting extended missions without frequent recharging. The energy management system includes a power monitoring feature that alerts the operator when battery levels are low, enabling timely recharging or battery replacement.
[0040] The robotic system is designed for deployment in various applications, including search and rescue missions, industrial inspections, and surveillance operations. In disaster response scenarios, the robot can navigate through rubble and confined spaces to locate survivors, assess structural integrity, and transmit real-time visual data to rescue teams. The ability to operate in hazardous environments without risking human lives makes the robotic system a valuable tool for emergency response agencies. In industrial settings, the robot can inspect pipelines, machinery, and hazardous workspaces, providing detailed visual and sensor-based assessments of structural conditions. This reduces the need for human intervention in dangerous environments, enhancing safety and efficiency. For surveillance applications, the robotic system offers a discreet and mobile monitoring solution, capable of navigating through security-sensitive areas and providing continuous real-time monitoring.
[0041] The durability of the robotic system has been tested across different environmental conditions, including confined spaces, rugged terrains, and debris-filled areas. Experimental results demonstrate superior maneuverability, adaptability, and resilience in challenging environments. The system’s ability to traverse narrow passageways, climb over obstacles, and adjust its shape dynamically ensures effective operation in unpredictable settings. The integration of real-time data transmission further enhances its usability, allowing operators to make informed decisions based on accurate and up-to-date information.
[0042] Overall, the present invention provides a highly flexible, efficient, and intelligent robotic solution for remote inspection, search and rescue, and surveillance applications. By integrating bioinspired biomechanics, RF communication, real-time visual monitoring, modular adaptability, and sensor-driven autonomy, the robotic system overcomes the limitations of traditional robots and offers a versatile tool for mission-critical operations. The innovative combination of mobility, intelligence, and real-time communication ensures that the robotic system is well-suited for deployment in complex and hazardous environments, providing a reliable and effective solution for modern robotic applications.

PBS buffer saline (pH 7.4) was prepared using 80 mL of distilled water, 2.02 g Na2HPO4.7H2O, and 0.3 g NaH2PO4.H2O. The pH was adjusted using HCl or NaOH and was made up to a volume of 100 mL. The adult insects were pricked with the 1:1 mixture of heat-killed bacterial preparation of E. coli and M. luteus in the ventral abdominal region for the immunized group. After immunization, beetles were fed and kept at normal environmental conditions. The hemolymph was collected 24 h post-immunization. The hemolymph was collected as per Haselton and Fridell, described in the study, and transferred into a pre-chilled Eppendorf having an equal proportion of protease inhibitors cocktail with 0.5 M EDTA solution. The hemolymph was mixed thoroughly and stored at -20 °C until further analysis (Lemaitre et al., 1997; Haselton and Fridell (2011).

To this volume, 10 mL phosphoric acid was added, and the solution was made up to 100 mL by double-distilled water. The prepared CBBG dye solution was double filtered. The dye was stored at 4 °C and kept in the dark bottle protected from light. A 0.8 mL dye reagent was added to 0.2 mL of hemolymph and controls. The hemolymph sample, both immunized and non-immunized with and without Tris-HCl were taken for the study. BSA as positive and distilled water as negative control were subjected to estimate the total protein concentration by Bradford’s assay absorption calibration curve (Bradford, 1976) using Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) as standard (1 mg. mL-1) [Hi-media, Mumbai, India]. In an embodiment of the invention disclosed, the four combinations of peptide-protein interactions for the AMPs, comprises, (a) ) L18-R4 (L- ligand, R-Receptor), the peptide binds with the cell wall adhesion EAP1 (Figure 4). The mode of action of AMPs was previously thought to be non-specific, leading to a rapid physical breakdown of microbial cell membranes, which results in cell leakage and death. Numerous AMPs have been shown to specifically interact with the fungal cell wall and/or cell membrane and have been linked to several sphingolipids and phospholipids. Either peptides can be absorbed by the fungal cell after interacting with the target or they can remain outside. Antifungal peptides can affect intracellular targets regardless of their potential for uptake, which can lead to a variety of effects, including the production of ROS, apoptosis, mitochondrial dysfunction, disruption of cation, homeostasis, cell cycle impairment, ATP efflux, autophagy, and vacuolar dysfunction.
(b) L18-R6, the peptide binds to protein Dolichyl phosphate mannose (DPM) (Figure 3). Enzymes that are bound to membranes may operate differently depending on cell membrane fluidity. Activated DPM is used for the glycosylation of surface proteins in the cell membrane. It is also an integral membrane protein. Thus, binding of the peptide to the protein disrupts the glycosylation process, making it the mechanism for the antimicrobial effect and a potent target for building antifungals.
(c) L18-R11, the formation of hyphae is a crucial step in the infection process because it aids in tissue penetration in host epithelial and endothelial cells and prevents the host immune system response. These glycosylphosphatidylinisotol anchored hyphal wall protein-2 were functionally and ontologically associated with signal transduction, filamentous growth, MAPK signalling, kinase activity, etc. that were targeted by the peptide sequence (Figure 4). Thus, the binding of peptides with hyphal proteins makes them a potential target for the prevention of hyphal formation as well as confirms the target for exploitation to develop new antifungals.

(d) L18-R13, Figure 5 shows how the peptide binds to the protein Mannan endo-1,6-alpha-mannosidase DFG5. The cell wall of C. albicans comprises ß-glucan, chitin, and mannoproteins. It is required for normal synthesis of the cell wall and alkaline pH-induced hyphal formation. The cell wall serves as the point of contact between the pathogen and host, and several cell wall proteins are involved in adhesion, a crucial component of virulence. It also has a variety of targets for pharmacological or vaccine therapy, because it is a crucial pathogen-specific structure (Spreghini et al., 2003; Navarro-Garcia et al., 2001; Sundstrom, 2002; Tkacz and DiDomenico,  2001).

COMPOSITE ELECTRODE FOR SUPERCAPACITORS TO ENHANCE ELECTROCHEMICAL PERFORMANCE A composite electrode for supercapacitors is provided to enhance electrochemical performance. The electrode comprises a composite material (220), a binding agent, a slurry (102), and a substrate. The composite material (220) is formed by probe sonication of 5 grams (g) to 20 gof black phosphorus (BP) and 5 g to 20 gof manganese (III) oxide (Mn₂O₃) nanoparticles (210)in a ratio of about 1:1, where Mn₂O₃ nanoparticles (210) is synthesized via a co-precipitation method and BP is exfoliated from bulk crystals using sonication. The binding agent consists of activated carbon, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF), and 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP). The slurry consists of BP-Mn₂O₃ composite, activated carbon, and polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) in a ratio of 8:1:1.The substrate, nickel foam (104), is coated with the slurry (102) using a drop-casting method and dried at 60°C for 12 hours. The resulting composite electrode demonstrates enhanced electrochemical performance, including improved capacitance, stability, and energy storage, making it suitable for advanced supercapacitor applications. Description of the Related Art
[0002] Energy storage technologies are critical for modern applications, including portable electronics, renewable energy systems, and electric vehicles. Among these technologies, supercapacitors have gained significant attention due to their high-power density, rapid charge-discharge capability, and excellent cycle life. However, achieving high energy density while maintaining superior electrochemical performance remains a challenge.
[0003] An existing solution(CN118458714A)discloses a composite electrode material for supercapacitors, integrating black phosphorus (BP) and conductive carbon nitride (C₃N₄). BP is synthesized using a high-energy ball milling method, while C₃N₄ is prepared through a molten salt reduction process. The composite exhibits high cyclic and structural stability, demonstrating supercapacitor behavior.
[0004] Another existing solution(CN118028600A) describes a method for synthesizing BP/transition metal composites by recycling lithium batteries using unmodified BP nanosheets. The recycled composite is applied in energy storage and conversion systems.Another existing solution(CN115101354BB) outlines a preparation method for graphene/BP composite fibers using a wet spinning process. The flexible fibrous supercapacitor, assembled with PVA-H₃PO₄ gel electrolytes, offers high capacitance and flexibility.
[0005] Yet another existing solution(CN113889604BB) reveals an organic intercalation method utilizing ultrasonic treatment to form BP-negative electrode material, which finds applications in magnesium-ion batteries.Yet another existing solution(US11,488,788B2) focuses on an electrolyte for supercapacitors, comprising ZnCl₂, tetraethylammonium tetrafluoroborate, and propylene carbonate. BP and zinc layers are utilized as electrode materials, achieving 70.16% capacitance retention over 9,500 cycles.
[0006] Yet another existing solution(CN113725010BB) describes a method for preparing electro-patterned BP/graphene electrodes, enhancing their electrical properties.Yet another existing solution(CN112467120A) introduces a two-step substitution method to synthesize nitrogen-phosphorus-doped porous carbon-coated manganese dioxide (MnO₂). This composite exhibit high-rate capability and cycling stability in lithium-ion batteries.
[0007] Yet another existing solution(CN110690055BB) presents a filtering method to prepare flexible BP/molybdenum trioxide films, offering high capacitance, mechanical stability, and flexibility.Yet another existing solution(CN112110429BB) outlines an electrochemical process to synthesize BP nanosheets, known for their excellent stability in photoelectric devices.
[0008] Yet another existing solution(CN107343957BB) details the synthesis of BP/manganese dioxide composite nanomaterials using bovine serum albumin as a template via electrostatic adsorption. The material is applicable in photodynamic therapy, antitumor treatments, and singlet oxygen generation under laser irradiation.Yet another existing solution(KR102003605B1) introduces a manufacturing method for a chemically and physically stable BP-graphene composite, enhancing its practical applications.
[0009] Traditional electrode materials for supercapacitors, such as carbon-based materials, offer excellent conductivity and stability but often lack sufficient energy storage capacity. On the other hand, transition metal oxides exhibit pseudocapacitive behavior, allowing higher energy density, but their poor conductivity and structural stability during cycling limit their performance. Recent advancements in nanotechnology have introduced composite materials that synergistically combine the advantages of multiple components, offering a potential solution to these challenges.
[0010] Black phosphorus (BP), a layered material with high electrical conductivity and a tunable band gap, has emerged as a promising candidate for energy storage applications. Its layered structure facilitates charge transport, while its unique electronic properties enhance energy storage capacity. Similarly, manganese (III) oxide (Mn₂O₃), a transition metal oxide, exhibits excellent pseudocapacitive behavior, making it suitable for supercapacitor electrodes. However, the standalone use of these materials is limited by issues such as stability and scalability.
[0011] To address these limitations, there is a need fordeveloping a composite material of black phosphorus and Mn₂O₃ nanoparticles.

[0033] The composite electrode enhances the electrochemical performance of supercapacitors, particularly in alkaline environments and also improves charge storage capabilities.The composite electrode offers several advantages that make it highly effective for supercapacitor applications. By combining black phosphorus (BP) and manganese (III) oxide (Mn₂O₃) nanoparticles, the composite material takes advantage of the synergistic properties of these two components. BP facilitates efficient charge transport, while Mn₂O₃ provides excellent pseudocapacitive behavior, resulting in improved energy storage and power density.
[0034] The composite electrode exhibits high stability and durability, thanks to its robust nickel foam substrate, which ensures mechanical stability and strong adhesion of the composite material. Additionally, the optimized binding agent ratio (8:1:1) enhances the structural integrity of the electrode. The drying process at 60°C creates a uniform and durable coating, further improving its reliability.
[0035] The fabrication process of the composite electrode is simple, scalable, and cost-effective, employing techniques such as probe sonication, co-precipitation, and drop-casting. These methods ensure uniform dispersion of manganese (III) oxide nanoparticles and BP, resulting in consistent material properties and enhanced electrical conductivity. The composite electrode is also environmentally friendly, as it uses non-toxic solvents like 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) and reusable substrates, reducing its environmental impact.
[0036] The composite electrode combines the high energy density of BP with the high-rate capability of Mn₂O₃, making it suitable for applications requiring rapid charge-discharge cycles and sustained energy output. It demonstrates superior specific capacitance due to the effective combination of pseudocapacitive and conductive properties. This makes the composite electrode ideal for use in energy storage systems, portable electronics, and renewable energy applications.
[0037] The thermal and mechanical stability of the composite electrode is another key advantage. The controlled drying process at 60°C ensures thermal stability, while the nickel foam substrate provides mechanical strength, enabling the electrode to perform reliably under rigorous conditions. Furthermore, the fabrication method allows for easy customization, enabling adjustments in material composition, substrate types, and coating thickness to meet specific performance requirements.

GLUTEN-FREE MILLET-BASED BISCUIT COMPOSITION AND METHOD FOR PRODUCING THE SAME A gluten-free millet-based biscuit composition is provided. The composition includes 42% to 54% weight by weight (w/w) of first millet (sorghum flour), 28% to 36% w/w of a second millet (pearl grain flour), 10% to 30% w/w of a protein component (yellow split mung bean flour), 5% w/w of texturizer (maltodextrin), 12% w/w of a fibre component (inulin), 28% w/w of icing sugar, 20% w/w of butter, 15% w/w of palm oil, 0.6% w/w of baking powder, 0.6% w/w of baking soda, 1% w/w of salt, and 5.2% w/w of raising agent. The food composition is baked in a baking oven at a temperature of 170 ºC for 10 to 20 minutes to form into the millet-based biscuit. Description:BACKGROUND
Technical Field
[0001] The embodiments herein generally relate to food compositions and more particularly, to a gluten-free millet-based biscuit composition. The embodiments further relate to a method for producing the gluten-free millet-based biscuit composition.
Description of the Related Art
[0002] Gluten-based biscuits dominate the market, but they are unsuitable for individuals with gluten intolerance or celiac disease. This has led to a rising demand for gluten-free alternatives, particularly millet-based biscuits, due to their high nutritional value and suitability for gluten-sensitive consumers.
[0003] While millet-based biscuits are available, they often face challenges related to poor texture, low protein content, and suboptimal organoleptic properties. Existing formulations incorporate various millets and plant/animal protein sources, but they frequently lack the crispness, mouthfeel, and sensory appeal required for widespread consumer acceptance.
[0004] Therefore, there is a need to develop a biscuit composition with enhanced nutritional and sensory qualities while maintaining a stable biscuit structure.
SUMMARY
[0005] In view of the foregoing, an embodiment herein provides a food composition for producing a millet-based biscuit. The food composition includes (i) a first millet that includes 42% to 54% weight by weight (w/w) of sorghum flour; (ii) a second millet that includes 28% to 36% w/w of pearl grain flour; (iii) a protein component that includes 10% to 30% w/w of yellow split mung bean flour. The first millet, the second millet, and the protein component are mixed together to form a millet mixture and the millet mixture is formed into the millet-based biscuit that has a synergistic effect of providing enhanced texture, organoleptic properties, and nutritional profile.
[0006] In some embodiments, the food composition includes a texturizer that includes 5% w/w of maltodextrin, and a fibre component that includes 12% w/w of inulin.
[0007] In some embodiments, the food composition includes one or more food additives that includes 28% w/w of icing sugar; 20% w/w of butter; 15% w/w of palm oil; 0.6% w/w of baking powder; 0.6% w/w of baking soda; 1% w/w of salt; and 5.2% w/w of raising agent.
[0008] In some embodiments, the food composition includes 48 grams (g) of sorghum flour, 32 g of pearl grain flour, 20 g of yellow split mung bean flour, 20 g of unsalted butter, 15 g of palm oil, 28 g of icing sugar, 5 g of maltodextrin, 12 g of inulin 12 g, 5.2 g of raising agent INS 500, 1 g of sea salt, 0.6 g of baking soda, and 0.6 g of baking powder.
[0009] In some embodiments, the food composition is baked in a baking oven at a temperature of 170 ºC for 10 to 20 minutes to form into the millet-based biscuit.
[0010] In some embodiments, the millet-based biscuit has a hardness of 1163 g on a first break and 675 g on a second break, a cohesiveness of 0.22, a springiness of 1.1 mm, and an adhesion of 0.6 mJ, indicating a firm yet crumbly texture with minimal stickiness.
[0011] In some embodiments, the millet-based biscuit includes 9.10% to 22.76% of crude protein, and 12.09% to 15.63% of crude fat.
[0012] In some embodiments the millet-based biscuit has a shelf-life of about 3-4 months at ambient conditions.
[0013] In one aspect, a method for producing a millet-based biscuit is provided. The method includes (i) beating 20% weight by weight (w/w) of an unsalted butter with 15% w/w of palm oil for 5 to 10 minutes to obtain a first mixture; (ii) adding 28% w/w of an icing sugar with the first mixture to obtain a second mixture; (iii) adding 5% of a texturizer comprising maltodextrin, and 12% w/w of a fibre component comprising inulin with the second mixture to obtain a third mixture, the fibre component is hydrated with 10 mL of water in the third mixture; (iv) mixing a first millet including 42% to 54% w/w of sorghum flour, a second millet including 28% to 36% w/w of pearl grain flour, and a protein component including 10% to 30% w/w of yellow split mung bean flour to obtain a millet mixture, where the millet mixture is added with 15% w/w of sea salt, 0.6% w/w of baking soda and 0.6% w/w of baking powder; (v) blending the millet mixture with the third mixture to obtain a fourth mixture, 5.2 g of raising agent INS 500 is added with the fourth mixture to obtain a dough mixture, the dough mixture is incubated at a temperature of 4ºC for 15 minutes; and (iv) baking the dough mixture in a desired shape in an oven at a temperature of 170 ºC for 10 to 20 minutes to form into the millet-based biscuit that has enhanced texture and organoleptic properties.
[0014] In some embodiments, the fibre component is hydrated with 10 mL of water in the third mixture; and the raising agent INS 500 is hydrated with 5 mL of water in the fourth mixture.
[0015] The gluten-free, protein-fortified millet biscuit of the present disclosure has enhanced nutritional and sensory properties, addressing the limitations of existing millet-based biscuits. The incorporation of yellow split mung bean flour significantly improves protein content, texture, and organoleptic appeal, making it suitable for individuals with gluten intolerance and celiac disease. The use of maltodextrin enhances dough consistency and reduces hardness, while inulin acts as a dietary fiber and binder, contributing to improved texture and structural stability. This optimized formulation ensures better crispness, mouthfeel, and consumer acceptance, making it a nutritionally superior and market-ready gluten-free biscuit alternative.

[0023] As mentioned, there remains a need for developing a biscuit composition with enhanced nutritional and sensory qualities while maintaining a stable biscuit structure. Various embodiments disclosed herein provide a gluten-free millet-based biscuit composition that has enhanced texture and organoleptic properties. Referring now to the drawings, and more particularly to FIGS. 1 through 4, where similar reference characters denote corresponding features consistently throughout the figures, preferred embodiments are shown.
[0024] FIG. 1 is a tabular view that illustrates a food composition for producing a millet-based biscuit according to some embodiments herein. The food composition includes a first millet, a second millet, and a protein component. The food composition further includes a texturizer, a fibre component, and one or more food additives. 
[0025] The first and second millets are rich in protein, fiber, vitamins, and minerals and form the core structural and nutritional base of the millet-based biscuit. In some embodiments, the first millet is sorghum flour. The first millet or the sorghum flour is in a concentration of 42% to 54% weight by weight (w/w) in the food composition. In some embodiments, the first millet is in a concentration of 48% w/w. The second millet is pearl grain flour. The second millet or the pearl grain flour is in a concentration of 28% to 36% w/w in the food composition. In some embodiments, the second millet is in a concentration of 32% w/w. In some embodiments, other gluten-free millets, such as finger millet (ragi), foxtail millet, barnyard millet, little millet, kodo millet, proso millet, and brown top millet, can be used in combination with at least one the first millet or the second millet to make the millet-based biscuit, where the concentration of the first millet may remain same or majority.
[0026] The protein component may be added as a protein source to enhance the nutritional value. In some embodiments, the protein component is flour. The protein component or yellow split mung bean flour is added in a concentration of 10% to 30% w/w in the food composition. In some embodiments, the protein component is in a concentration of 20% w/w. In some embodiments, other protein components such as chickpea flour, green gram flour, lentil flour, pea protein isolate, soy flour, quinoa flour, bean amaranth flour, pumpkin seed protein, jackfruit seed, groundnut and almond flour can be used in place of the yellow split mung bean floor.
[0027] The texturizer may be incorporated into the food composition to enhance dough consistency and reduce biscuit hardness. The texturizer may be selected from a group consisting of maltodextrin, modified starch, guar gum, xanthan gum, inulin, and pectin. In some embodiments, the texturizer is maltodextrin. The texturizer may be added in a concentration of 5% w/w in the food composition.
[0028] The fibre component may be incorporated into the food composition to enhance dietary fiber content, improve dough binding, and contribute to the overall texture and structure of the biscuit. The fibre component may be selected from a group consisting of maltodextrin, psyllium husk, oat fiber, apple fiber,  and resistant starch. In some embodiments, the fibre component is inulin. The fibre component may be added in a concentration of 12% w/w in the food composition.
[0029] The one or more food additives includes icing sugar, butter, palm oil, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and raising agent. The one or more food additives may be added to provide sweetness, richness, and crispness, while also enhancing texture, shelf life, flavor, and volume. 
[0030] The icing sugar may act as a sweetener and is added to the food composition in a concentration of 28% w/w. Other sweeteners such as coconut sugar, date sugar, stevia powder, erythritol, xylitol, jaggery and maple sugar may be added in place of icing sugar.
[0031] The butter may act as a fat source and enhance flavor, richness, and mouthfeel, while contributing to crispness. The butter may be salted butter and is added to the food composition in a concentration of 20% w/w. Ghee, margarine, coconut oil, olive oil, and vegetable shortening may be added in place of butter.
[0032] The palm oil may also act as the fat source and improves texture, shelf life, and biscuit structure. The palm oil is added to the food composition in a concentration of 15% w/w. Other fat sources such as coconut oil, sunflower oil, soybean oil, canola oil, and vegetable shortening may be added in place of palm oil.
[0033] The baking powder may act as a leavening agent, helping the biscuit achieve a light and airy texture, and is added to the food composition in a concentration of 0.6% w/w. Other leavening agents such as cream of tartar and self-raising flour may be used in place of baking powder.
[0034] The baking soda may function as a leavening and pH regulator, aiding in biscuit expansion and browning, and is added to the food composition in a concentration of 0.6% w/w. Other alternatives such as potassium bicarbonate and ammonium bicarbonate may be used in place of baking soda. The salt may act as a flavor enhancer and dough strengthener, balancing taste and regulating gluten-free flour structure, and is added to the food composition in a concentration of 1% w/w. Other salt alternatives such as sea salt, Himalayan salt, and low-sodium salt substitutes may be used in place of salt (sodium chloride).
[0035] The raising agent may facilitate leavening, contributing to the desired texture and volume of the biscuit, and is added to the food composition in a concentration of 5.2% w/w. In some embodiments, the raising agent is ammonium bicarbonate INS 503. Other raising agents such as yeast, and baking blends may be used in place of the ammonium bicarbonate INS 503.
[0036] In some embodiments, the food composition comprises 48 grams (g) of sorghum flour, 32 g of pearl grain flour, 20 g of yellow split mung bean flour, 20 g of unsalted butter, 15 g of palm oil, 28 g of icing sugar, 5 g of maltodextrin, 12 g of inulin, 5.2 g of raising agent INS 500, 1 g of sea salt, 0.6 g of baking soda, and 0.6 g of baking powder.
[0037] The food composition is formulated or formed into the millet-based biscuit. The ingredients of the food composition are mixed together to obtain a dough mixture. The dough mixture may be sheeted and cut into a desired shape. The cut pieces are baked in a baking oven at a temperature of 170 ºC for 10 to 20 minutes to form into the millet-based biscuit. The millet-based biscuit is gluten-free.
[0038] The millet-based biscuit has a synergistic effect of providing enhanced texture and organoleptic properties. The millet-based biscuit has a texture profile including hardness of 1163 g on a first break and 675 g on a second break, a cohesiveness of 0.22, a springiness of 1.1 mm, and an adhesion of 0.6 mJ, indicating a firm yet crumbly texture with minimal stickiness. The millet-based biscuit also has improved nutritional profile including 9.10% to 22.76% of crude protein, and 12.09% to 15.63% of crude fat.
[0039] The millet-based biscuit is shelf-stable and has a shelf-life of about 3-4 months. The millet-based biscuit may have storage stability and storable at ambient conditions for a long period of time (i.e. upto 4 months) with a modified atmospheric packaging.
[0040] FIGS. 2A-2B are flow diagrams that illustrate a method for producing a millet-based biscuit using a food composition of FIG. 1 according to some embodiments herein. At step 202, 20% weight by weight (w/w) of an unsalted butter is beaten with 15% w/w of palm oil for 5 to 10 minutes to obtain a first mixture. Beating is performed until a smooth texture is obtained. At step 204, 28% w/w of an icing sugar is added with the first mixture to obtain a second mixture. The icing sugar may be sieved with 75 microns sieve, ASTM No. 200 before adding with the first mixture. At step 206, 5% of a texturizer, and 12% w/w of a fibre component are added with the second mixture to obtain a third mixture. The fibre component is hydrated with 10 mL of water in the third mixture. The texturizer is maltodextrin and the fibre component is inulin. 
[0041] At step 208, 42% to 54% w/w of a first millet, 28% to 36% w/w of a second millet, and 10% to 30% w/w of a protein component are mixed together to obtain a millet mixture. The first millet is sorghum flour, the second millet is pearl grain flour, and the protein component is yellow split mung bean flour. At step 210, 15% w/w of sea salt, 0.6% w/w of baking soda and 0.6% w/w of baking powder are added with the millet mixture. At step 212, the millet mixture is blended with the third mixture to obtain a fourth mixture.
[0042] At step 214, 5.2 g of raising agent INS 500 is added with the fourth mixture to obtain a dough mixture. The raising agent INS 500 is hydrated with 5 mL of water in the fourth mixture. At step 216, the dough mixture is incubated at a temperature of 4ºC for 15 minutes. At step 218, the dough mixture is sheeted and cut into a desired shape to obtain one or more cut pieces. The sheeted dough mixture may be cut in a circular die cutter with an inner diameter of 7 cm. At step 220, the dough mixture in the desired shape is baked in an oven at a temperature of 170 ºC for 10 to 20 minutes to obtain the millet-based biscuit.
[0043] The baked millet-based biscuits are cooled at a temperature of 25ºC for 15 mins and packed in a multilayer flexible packaging with a heat seal for further use.

[0047] Characterization of biscuits
[0048] Texture profile analysis
[0049] The Texture Profile Analysis (TPA) is conducted on baked biscuits formulated with food compositions (batch 1-13) of Table 1, including wheat (100%), sorghum (100%), pearl millet (100%) control biscuits, and commercial biscuits made from whole wheat and millets. The analysis is performed using a Texture Profile Analyzer (Brookfield CT3 model) with a TA 39 (2 mm cylindrical probe) and the TA-P-KIT2 and TA-BT-KIT fixture base table in manual mode. The test parameters include: TPA mode (2 cycles), auto trigger load (4g), deformation (5.0 mm), and speed (0.5 mm/s).
[0050] The texture profile parameters such as hardness, springiness, cohesiveness, and adhesion are measured in duplicates and depicted in Table 2. [0052] As detailed in Table 2, a comparative analysis of all formulations, including commercial millet and whole wheat biscuits, reveals that the texture of Batches 10 and 11 closely resembles commercial millet biscuits.
[0053] Colour estimation
[0054] FIG. 4 shows results on color estimation of biscuits formulated with food compositions (Batches 1-13) according to some embodiments herein. The color estimation includes lightness, redness, and yellowness of all biscuit batch formulations (Batch 1-13) and commercial biscuit products made from whole wheat, refined wheat flour, and millets. The analysis is conducted using the CIELAB system of the HunterLab color estimator, standardized with white and black tiles. All samples are measured in triplicates.
[0055] As shown in FIG. 4, the color estimation analysis reveals that Batches 10 and 11 align with the color characteristics of commercial millet and whole wheat biscuits.
[0056] Nutritional proximate analysis
[0057] The crude protein estimation for mung bean powder and biscuit batches B10, B11, and B12 is conducted using the Kjeldahl Method (AOAC 991.36). The digestion is performed in a Magnus KBD083 Kjeldahl block digester, followed by distillation in an Oracle KDI010 Kjeldahl Distillation unit. The crude fat estimation of B10, B11, and B12 is analyzed using the Soxhlet extraction method (AOAC 955.04) in a SoxTRON Sox-2 apparatus with petroleum ether as the solvent. Abstract:

The present invention relates to a hybrid ultra-wideband (UWB) and LiDAR-powered smart footwear system designed to assist visually impaired individuals in navigation. The system comprises a pair of footwear (102A-B) integrated with LiDAR sensors (104A-N) for spatial mapping and obstacle detection, a UWB receiver (106) for precise indoor positioning, a microcontroller (108) for real-time data processing, a feedback unit (112) for haptic and auditory alerts, and a rechargeable power source (110). Description:BACKGROUND
Technical Field
[0001] The present invention relates to the field of assistive navigation technologies and, more specifically, to a hybrid ultra-wideband (UWB) and LiDAR-powered smart footwear system designed for visually impaired individuals.

Description of the Related Art 
[0002] The navigational aids for visually impaired individuals have seen significant advancements in recent years, leveraging deep learning, object recognition, and sensor-based technologies. Existing solutions, such as smart blind sticks, wearable assistance devices, and vision-based navigation systems, aim to enhance spatial awareness and obstacle detection. However, these technologies present several limitations that impact their effectiveness in real-world scenarios. Many systems rely on camera-based object detection (e.g., YOLO, CNN), which can be highly dependent on lighting conditions and may struggle in low-light or high-glare environments. Additionally, depth estimation techniques using monocular cameras or stereo vision often lack the precision required for accurate distance measurement, leading to potential navigation errors.
[0003] Audio-based feedback mechanisms, while useful, can overload the user’s cognitive senses, making real-time decision-making challenging. Some solutions rely solely on ultrasonic or infrared sensors, which provide limited range and lower accuracy, particularly in detecting complex or dynamic obstacles. Furthermore, indoor navigation remains a challenge, as GPS-based systems are ineffective in enclosed spaces like shopping malls, airports, or office buildings. While some assistive devices integrate haptic feedback, their implementations are often limited in adaptability, offering basic vibration alerts without context-aware prioritization. Additionally, existing mobility aids lack an integrated, multi-sensory approach that effectively combines real-time mapping, precise localization, and adaptive feedback for seamless navigation. These shortcomings highlight the need for an advanced assistive system that overcomes environmental limitations, enhances obstacle detection accuracy, and improves indoor positioning while maintaining ease of use, comfort, and adaptability for visually impaired users.
[0004] To address the aforementioned technical drawbacks in existing technologies, there arises a need to provide an advanced assistive system that enhances navigation and situational awareness for visually impaired individuals.

Contextual AI models, which leverage real-time environmental data, user behavior, and predictive analytics, play a crucial role in optimizing smart home ecosystems by personalizing automation, enhancing security, and improving energy management. Despite the transformative potential, several challenges hinder seamless adoption, including data privacy concerns, interoperability among heterogeneous IoT devices, and the computational demands of AI inference. This study addresses these limitations and explores emerging solutions such as federated learning for privacy-preserving AI, blockchain for secure data sharing, and edge AI to minimize latency and reduce cloud dependency. The future of smart homes will increasingly rely on decentralized, context-aware AI systems capable of learning from user interactions while safeguarding sensitive data. By integrating contextual AI models into smart home IoT infrastructures, the next generation of intelligent living spaces will become more intuitive, secure, and energy-efficient. This research underscores the importance of adaptive AI frameworks in driving seamless human-AI interaction, ultimately redefining the way smart homes enhance everyday life.

Contextual AI enables smart homes to move beyond basic automation by integrating natural language processing (NLP) for voice and conversational interactions, computer vision for human activity recognition, and machine learning to dynamically adjust system behavior based on user preferences and historical data. The Role of Contextual AI in Smart Homes
Contextual AI enables smart home systems to go beyond simple task automation and evolve into intelligent ecosystems capable of real-time decision-making based on user behavior, environmental conditions, and predictive analytics. Unlike rule-based systems, which rely on fixed commands, contextual AI continuously learns from sensor inputs and user interactions to anticipate needs and autonomously optimize home operations.
Several AI-driven technologies contribute to context-aware automation in smart homes:
• Natural Language Processing (NLP): Facilitates seamless voice-based interactions, enabling users to control smart devices through natural speech commands. NLP-powered virtual assistants, such as Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant, are continuously evolving to better understand contextual nuances and personalize responses based on user preferences and past interactions.
• Computer Vision: Plays a critical role in human activity recognition, gesture control, and security monitoring. AI-driven cameras can distinguish between authorized residents and unknown visitors, detect falls or unusual movements, and enable automated access control based on facial recognition.
• Machine Learning (ML): Adapts smart home behavior dynamically by analyzing historical data, behavioral patterns, and environmental changes. For example, ML-powered climate control systems can learn user temperature preferences and automatically adjust thermostat settings for energy efficiency.
• Sensor Fusion and Edge AI: IoT-enabled motion detectors, temperature sensors, smart appliances, and wearables provide real-time data streams that allow AI models to anticipate user needs and automate household operations, such as adjusting lighting, regulating indoor air quality, and optimizing energy consumption.
By integrating multi-modal sensor data, contextual AI can create a more immersive and intuitive living environment, allowing smart homes to function autonomously, proactively, and intelligently.

Device Control and Communication
1. Smart Lights and Plugs Control via Web Service
o Control Service Implementation:
The assistant interacts with smart lights (Philips Hue) and plugs (TP-Link) through a dedicated control service. This service is a web-based application built using Node.js.
o API Libraries:
 Philips Hue: The communication with the Philips Hue Bridge is handled via the node-hue-api library. This library allows the control service to send commands to and receive status updates from the Hue Bridge, enabling operations like turning lights on/off, adjusting brightness, or changing colors.
 TP-Link Plugs: Similarly, the tplink-smarthome-api library is used to interface with TP-Link smart plugs. This API library provides functionalities to manage the plugs—turning them on or off, scheduling operations, and monitoring energy consumption.
2. Other Device Updates via Message Queuing
o AMQP and RabbitMQ Integration:
For devices beyond the smart lights and plugs, the system relies on the Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) and RabbitMQ queues.
 Data Flow:
Each device periodically sends its status and telemetry data to RabbitMQ queues. This is achieved using SCoT—a dedicated component that collects data from the devices and publishes it into one or more queues.
 Listening to Queues:
The assistant listens to these RabbitMQ queues to keep the state information of the various devices up to date. By consuming these messages, the system remains aware of the latest sensor readings and device statuses.
3. Device Control via SCoT
o Control Requests:
When a control command needs to be issued to a device that isn’t directly managed by the web service (i.e., devices that don’t have a direct API integration), the assistant sends a control request to SCoT.
o Command Relay:
SCoT receives the control request and relays it to the appropriate device. This approach decouples the command issuance from direct device communication, providing a flexible and scalable mechanism for device management.

Conversely, if the water hardness falls below a specific threshold, an alert is triggered, prompting an email warning and advising the activation of the water softener.

Challenges in Implementing Contextual AI in Smart Homes
Despite its transformative potential, several key challenges and limitations hinder the seamless adoption of contextual AI in smart home IoT systems:
1. Data Privacy and Security Concerns:
o Smart homes rely on the continuous collection of sensitive personal data, including voice recordings, biometric information, and real-time activity logs.
o Unauthorized access, cyber threats, and data breaches pose significant privacy risks, making it imperative to implement robust encryption, authentication mechanisms, and privacy-preserving AI techniques such as federated learning and differential privacy.
2. Interoperability and Standardization Issues:
o The lack of universal protocols and cross-platform compatibility among IoT devices makes integration challenging.
o Smart home ecosystems often consist of devices from different manufacturers, each using proprietary communication protocols, requiring standardized APIs and middleware solutions for seamless interoperability.

Description:An air conditioning (AC) unit works by removing heat from indoor air and releasing it outside, thereby cooling and dehumidifying the indoor environment. The internal unit (1.1) sucks the indoor hot air and in turn blows cold dehumidified air indoor. It operates on the principle of refrigeration using a closed-loop system with a refrigerant. The compressor (1.3), located in the outdoor unit, compresses the low-pressure, low-temperature refrigerant gas into a high-pressure, high-temperature gas. This compression increases the energy level of the refrigerant. The hot, high-pressure gas moves to the condenser coil (outdoor unit) (1.4). A fan blows air over the coils (1.5), helping the refrigerant release heat to the outside air. As the refrigerant loses heat, it condenses into a high-pressure liquid. The high-pressure liquid refrigerant passes through an expansion valve (1.6), which reduces its pressure. As pressure drops, the refrigerant becomes a low-pressure, low-temperature liquid-gas mixture. The cold refrigerant enters the evaporator coil (indoor unit) (1.2). Warm indoor air is blown over the evaporator coil, transferring heat from the air to the refrigerant. The refrigerant evaporates into a low-pressure gas, absorbing heat and cooling the air. A fan then circulates the cooled air back into the room. The low-pressure refrigerant gas returns to the compressor, and the cycle repeats. Thermostat controls the temperature by turning the AC on and off as needed. Filter cleans the air by trapping dust and pollutants.
